Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — the test-first evidence slice. It measures and pins the divergence between the headless arena's mineral supply and the shipped game's economy **before** any arena change.

# Goal

As the project, I want the arena-vs-game mineral divergence measured, recorded and reproducible from a command, so the "perfect-collection ceiling" of 7.67 / 5.53 is evidenced as a harness artefact (or not) instead of being asserted in prose.

# Target outcome

A deterministic measurement — an executable test plus a short written record — of both economies:

- **Arena (real-supply mode, campaign/one-level):** a static field of `spawns.minerals × 3` = 18 points (`DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS.minerals = 6`), topped back up to 6 every `COLLECTABLE_RESPAWN_TICKS` (150) from that same reservoir; `nextMineral` only decrements, and **no mineral is dropped on a kill** (`realSupplyMode` pushes only power-ups).
- **Shipped game:** no seeded field (`PlayScene.resetRunState` sets `this.minerals = []`); minerals come only from `resolveMineralKillPayout` — `2 × round(collected + bonus[0.25–1.25])` per non-asteroid kill, 2 per small asteroid — so a level-1 five-wave sortie (42 enemies) supplies ≈63 minerals from kills.

Recorded for each ring's aggression-selected level: the per-sortie mineral availability under the arena's model and under the game's kill-drop model, with the exact command that reproduces both.

# Definition of done

- A test in `src/ai/eval/` (e.g. `arenaMineralEconomy.test.ts`) measures the arena's per-sortie mineral supply in real-supply mode and asserts the documented figure, and measures the game-equivalent kill-drop supply for the same sortie (enemy count × the shared rule's expected payout) and asserts the divergence — both from seeded runs, no wall clock.
- The mechanism (static reservoir with no kill-drops vs kill-drop-only) and the measured per-sortie figures at ring-1 and ring-2 levels are recorded in a comment on this item and in the arena's documented fidelity boundary (`docs/BALANCING.md`) with the reproducing command.
- Every assertion carries a comment naming why its expected value is the one it is.
- The measurement is deterministic: same seed ⇒ identical figures.

# Constraints

- **Read-only evidence.** No arena behaviour change, no drop-rate change and no balance change in this slice.
- Do not re-pin any existing guard; the measurement is additive evidence.
- Test scope follows `/skill:test`; never invoke a test command directly.

# Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the mineral reservoir (`buildSpawnPlan` / `seededFieldPoints`), `nextMineral` and the real-supply kill seam (`destroyHostile`).
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — `DEFAULT_ARENA_SPAWNS` / `ArenaSpawns`.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the shared kill-drop rule the game-equivalent figure mirrors.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` (the doubled payout and its bonus roll).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the one-level runner that builds the shipped five-wave sortie.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the arena's documented fidelity boundaries.

# Acceptance Criteria

- The arena's per-sortie mineral availability and the shipped game's kill-drop availability are both measured for the ring-1 and ring-2 aggression-selected levels, with the mechanism recorded and the reproducing command stated.
- The measurement is an executable, deterministic test (seeded, no wall clock) whose assertions state why each expected figure is that figure.
- The divergence (arena static supply vs game kill-drop supply) is recorded in the arena's documented fidelity boundary with the command.
- No arena behaviour, drop rate or balance value changes in this slice, and no existing guard is re-pinned.
- Delivers parent AC: The **arena's per-sortie mineral availability is measured against the shipped game** — the mechanism (static 18-field with no kill-drops vs the game's kill-drop-only economy) and the per-sortie figure at each ring's aggression-selected level are both recorded with the command that reproduces them.
- Impact section recorded.

# Dependencies

None — first slice (test-first).

# Impact

The income harness's mineral under-supply becomes a measured, reproducible fact instead of a hypothesis, so the balance decision rests on evidence.

Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — the shared-core slice that gives the headless arena a seam into the game's real mineral payout without importing Phaser.

# Goal

As the project, I want the game's mineral kill-payout **decision** (re-drop count, deposit threshold, Salvage fold) to live in one Phaser-free module consumed by both the scene seam and the headless arena, so the arena can model the real rule and the two can never drift.

# Problem

`resolveMineralKillPayout` / `resolveMineralKillDrops` in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` construct Phaser `Mineral` display objects, so the headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, Node/vitest, no Phaser) cannot consume the rule. Today the arena therefore invents its own supply (a static 18-point field).

# Target outcome

- A pure, Phaser-free module (e.g. `src/core/mineralPayout.ts`) owning the payout **decision**: the doubled re-drop count (`MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER × round(collected + bonus)`), the deposit decision (`redropCount + salvageBonus ≥ MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD` ⇒ one deposit worth `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`), and the small-asteroid yield — all expressed as numbers, not game objects.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` consumes that decision and keeps its existing behaviour exactly (same draw order, same scatter, same deposit, same Salvage suppression) — the shared rule stays the single source of truth for the game and the gyms.
- The arena can import the decision module with no Phaser dependency.

# Definition of done

- The pure module has its own unit tests covering: the non-asteroid doubled count, a zero-collected bonus roll, the deposit threshold (including a surplus wreck paying one deposit), small vs large/medium asteroid, and the Salvage fold.
- `mineralKillDrops.ts` delegates to the pure module; its existing tests pass unchanged (behaviour-preserving refactor, no re-pinning).
- No new RNG draws are introduced: the bonus roll is exactly one draw per non-asteroid wreck, as today.
- Documentation (module doc comments, and `docs/BALANCING.md` where the rule is described) names the pure decision module as the single source.

# Constraints

- **Behaviour-preserving.** This slice must not change any game, gym or arena outcome; if a test pin moves, the refactor was not behaviour-preserving — fix the refactor, not the pin.
- No Phaser import in the pure module (guard it with a test that imports it in the headless environment).
- Determinism preserved: no wall-clock reads and no un-injected randomness in the pure decision (rng injected).

# Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the scene seam that will delegate to the pure module.
- `src/core/mineralPayout.ts` — the new Phaser-free decision module.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` / `collectMineral` (the rule's entity side).
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — the display object that stays Phaser-side.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the documented kill-drop rule.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A Phaser-free module owns the mineral kill-payout decision (count, deposit threshold, small-asteroid yield, Salvage fold) and is importable by the headless arena.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` delegates to it with **no** behaviour change: its existing tests pass unmodified and no game/gym/arena figure moves.
- Unit tests cover the doubled count, the bonus roll, the deposit threshold and its surplus rule, the asteroid tiers and the Salvage fold.
- The pure module has no Phaser import and no un-injected randomness or wall-clock read (asserted by a test).
- The single-source-of-truth relationship is documented in the module doc comment and in `docs/BALANCING.md`.
- Impact section recorded.

# Dependencies

Blocked by `Test: record the arena-vs-game mineral divergence` — the divergence evidence this refactor serves.

# Impact

The arena can measure the game's real mineral payout instead of a harness constant, without duplicating the rule.

Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — slice A of the fidelity fix: real-supply mode gets the game's kill-drop mineral economy instead of a static field.

# Goal

As a Hangar War player, I want a measured sortie to pay the minerals the game actually pays for the kills it made, so the between-sortie income the unlock tree was balanced against is measured on a faithful field.

# Target outcome

In **real-supply mode** (campaign and per-level/one-level runs) the arena's minerals come from kills through the shared rule — not from a seeded reservoir:

- `destroyHostile` resolves each wreck's payout through the Phaser-free decision module from the extraction slice (non-asteroid: `2 × round(collected + bonus)`; small asteroid: 2; large/medium asteroid: 0; a payout ≥ 10 becomes one 10-value deposit) and registers the resulting minerals on `world.minerals` at the wreck.
- Drop positions come from the seeded stream (mirroring the game's `scatterDoubledMineralDrops` layout), so same seed ⇒ byte-identical records.
- The static mineral reservoir and its 150-tick top-up are **not** used in real-supply mode; they stay exactly as they are for the seeded skirmish.
- `ArenaSpawns.minerals` is documented as skirmish-only; real-supply mode's mineral availability is enemy-count-driven.

# Definition of done

- Tests written first (red) pinning: no seeded mineral field in real-supply mode; the per-kill payout shapes above; the deposit at the threshold; determinism (byte-identical records, seeded draws only); the seeded skirmish unchanged.
- Every guard the model change moves (ring-timing budgets, income, churn, aim accuracy, experience targets, any other arena-derived pin) is re-pinned **deliberately in this commit**, each changed pin carrying a comment stating why the expected value changed and the before/after measurement.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`'s fidelity boundary now states that the arena models the real mineral kill-drop economy (and what remains approximated), and the arena's module doc comment matches.

Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — slice B of the fidelity fix: the game's absorb→re-drop loop.

# Goal

As the project, I want the arena's non-asteroid enemies to absorb the minerals they fly over, exactly as `BaseEnemy.collectMineral` does in the game, so a wreck's re-drop reflects the minerals that enemy swallowed and the arena's mineral supply matches the game's rather than only its first-order kill-drop count.

# Target outcome

- In real-supply mode a live non-asteroid hostile that overlaps a mineral absorbs it: the mineral leaves the field and the hostile's collected count increases by the mineral's value (1 for a dot, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE` for a red deposit), mirroring `collectMinerals` in `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`.
- Asteroids and lane-traffic hazards never absorb (they are inert / `collectMineral` no-ops in the game).
- The absorbed count feeds the kill payout (`2 × round(collected + bonus)`) through the same Phaser-free rule, so absorbed minerals are re-dropped at the wreck — the game's economy loop.
- A telemetry event records absorption (e.g. `mineral_absorbed`) so the effect is measurable without changing existing event shapes.

# Definition of done

- Tests written first (red) pinning: a hostile absorbs an overlapping mineral and its wreck then re-drops the absorbed count through the rule; an absorbed deposit is worth 10; asteroids absorb nothing; determinism preserved; the player's own collection is unaffected.
- Every guard the change moves is re-pinned in the same commit with a reason comment, and before/after figures recorded.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`'s fidelity boundary records absorption as modelled, with any remaining approximation (e.g. absorption radius, hostile avoidance behaviour) stated under the existing convention.
- The committed income artifact and GDD §8.2 figures are refreshed from the new model.

# Constraints

- **Mirror the game's rule, do not invent one** — reuse the game's collection semantics (overlap radius, value, asteroid exclusion); where the arena must approximate (hostiles are stationary), document it as a fidelity boundary rather than adding a new constant.
- **Determinism** — absorption consumes no new RNG draws.
- **No collection-routing change** and no game-side behaviour change.

# Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the per-tick mineral pass and the hostile model.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — the shared `collectMinerals` absorption semantics to mirror.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `collectMineral` / `mineralRedropCount`.
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — mineral `value` (dot vs deposit).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — income/pace guards to re-pin.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the arena fidelity boundary.

# Acceptance Criteria

- In real-supply mode a live non-asteroid hostile absorbs an overlapping mineral (value-aware: 10 for a deposit), asteroids absorb nothing, and the absorbed count feeds the kill re-drop through the shared rule.
- Absorption adds no RNG draws: same policy + config + seed ⇒ byte-identical records.
- A telemetry event makes absorption measurable and existing event shapes are unchanged.
- Every moved guard is re-pinned in the same commit with a comment stating why, and the before/after figures are recorded.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` documents absorption as modelled plus any remaining approximation; the committed income artifact and GDD §8.2 figures are refreshed.
- Delivers parent AC: **The arena's mineral supply is made faithful to the shipped game** so a measured run's mineral supply tracks the game's real kill-drop/absorption economy rather than a fixed 18-point field — **per the producer ruling (a), by modelling the game's kill-drop rule** (consuming the shared `resolveMineralKillPayout`/`mineralRedropCount` behaviour), with the approach recorded.
- Impact section recorded.

# Dependencies

Blocked by `Model the game's mineral kill-drops in the arena`.

# Impact

Enemy salvage behaviour stops being invisible to the income measurement, so the measured field behaves like the game's.

Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — the closing slice: measure the game-faithful income, rule on the 9.0 / 6.0 target, and lock the result in.

# Goal

As the designer/producer, I want a game-faithful seeds-1–3 measurement of per-deployment income with an explicit ruling on whether 9.0 (ring 1) / 6.0 (ring 2) is reached, so the balance point is a measured decision rather than a restated target.

# Target outcome

- `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level --income-out docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` run on the game-faithful arena (seeds 1–3, competent bot, shipped five-wave sortie), with ring-1 and ring-2 minerals/deployment and capture rates recorded before and after the fidelity fix.
- A **wider seed set** confirmation (beyond seeds 1–3) so a capture-rate or income conclusion is not read out of three seeds' variance; the wider set is recorded as evidence with its size and reason.
- An explicit **verdict**: either income moved toward 9.0 / 6.0, or the achievable ceiling is recorded as the accepted balance point with the reason — including how much of the residual gap is mineral availability versus collection routing versus capture rate.
- If the verdict indicates a further **economy-side** change (game spawn/drop rate or capture rate), it is **not** made here: file a linked follow-up work item carrying its own measurement, and record why.
- The committed artifact, the income guard and GDD §8.2 (table, verdict, unlock-pace rows) are re-pinned to the final measurement, each changed pin with a comment stating why.
- A **deterministic artifact-divergence guard** fails if `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` diverges from a fresh measurement of the shipped bot.

# Definition of done

- The final measurement is reproducible from the stated command, and the artifact is generated by the CLI, never hand-edited.
- The verdict (target reached vs accepted ceiling) is recorded on this item and in GDD §8.2 with the supporting figures.
- The wider seed set is recorded and the reason for its size stated.
- The artifact-divergence guard is deterministic (seeded, bounded runtime) and fails on a stale artifact.
- README / `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` are updated if they quote a changed figure.

# Constraints

- **Balance figures are measured, not guessed**; the artifact is the evidence.
- **No collection-routing change** (owned by `AH-0MWLLPA1Q0006U2P`) and no hangar-price or drop-rate change in this item.
- The divergence guard must not make the suite slow: bound it to the committed seeds and a single sortie per ring.
- The re-pin overlaps the sibling `AH-0MWLLPAQL003IEXE` (income artifact re-pin after the collection re-tune): re-pin to **this** item's measurement and note in a comment that the later routing re-tune will re-pin again — do not wait for it.

# Key Files

- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the regeneration CLI (`--one-level --income-out`).
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — the committed measurement artifact.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — income guard and the new artifact-divergence guard.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the one-level runner and income derivation.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §8.2 table, verdict and unlock-pace rows.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — any quoted income figure.

# Acceptance Criteria

- Seeds-1–3 income for ring 1 and ring 2 is recorded after the fidelity fix, with the before/after comparison and the reproducing command.
- A wider seed set confirms the result and is recorded with its size and reason.
- An explicit verdict records either movement toward 9.0 / 6.0 or the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point with the reason; any indicated economy-side change is filed as a linked follow-up item, not made here.
- The committed artifact is regenerated by the CLI; the income guard and GDD §8.2 (table, verdict, unlock pace) are re-pinned with a reason per changed pin.
- README / `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` quotes are updated where they cite a changed figure.
- Delivers parent AC: **Re-measured income** (seeds 1–3, competent bot, shipped five-wave sortie) is recorded for both rings, and either **moves ring-1/ring-2 minerals/deployment toward 9.0 / 6.0** or records the achievable ceiling as the accepted balance point with the reason.
- Delivers parent AC: Any further economy-side change (game spawn/drop rate or capture rate) is only considered **after** the fidelity fix and is backed by its own measurement; collection routing is **not** changed here (owned by AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J).
- Delivers parent AC: A deterministic guard fails if the committed income artifact diverges from a fresh measurement of the shipped bot (or the arena's mineral model diverges from its documented game-faithful contract).
- Delivers parent AC: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it quotes these figures) and the GDD.
- Delivers parent AC: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- Impact section recorded.

# Dependencies

Blocked by `Mirror enemy mineral absorption in the arena`.

# Impact

The between-sortie income the unlock tree is balanced on is measured on a game-faithful field, and the target is either met or replaced by a measured, stated balance point.

# Collection noises should indicate how full the hull is

## Problem statement

The player mineral pickup chime currently climbs one A-minor scale degree per collected mineral and restarts at the base note after 1.5 s of game time without a pickup, so its pitch reports **pickup tempo**, not **hull fullness**. A player cannot hear how close the hold is to full, and the same pitch can mean "first mineral of a fast streak" or "the hold is nearly full". The chime should instead report how full the hull is.

## Users

- **Player** — "I want the collection chime to tell me how full my hull is, so I know how close I am to the next power-up without looking at the HUD."
- **Player** — "A full hull should always sound the same note, and the note I hear on my first mineral should always be the same one, so the cue is learnable."
- **Developer / producer** — "I want the new mapping behind a feature flag that is on by default, so the old streak behaviour can be restored with one persisted flip if the feel is wrong."

## Acceptance Criteria

- The new feedback is behind a persisted feature flag (`hullFillMineralChime`) that defaults to **ON**, so the shipped build plays the fill-based chime and a persisted `false` restores today's streak behaviour.
- With the flag ON, the pitch of a player pickup is a **pure function of the hull's fill level after that pickup** — not of pickup tempo: the hold's first mineral always plays the fixed base note and a hold that has just reached capacity always plays the fixed top note, for every hold capacity (5, 10, 20, 40, …), level, scene and run.
- Within one hold the pitch never falls as the hold fills, a red deposit (`MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE` = 10) jumps the equivalent number of steps in one pickup, and resolving the hold (emptying it) returns the next pickup to the base note.
- The fill→pitch mapping is implemented **once** as a pure, unit-tested function in `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` and consumed by the single shared `CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected()` dispatch; `PlayScene` and every gym that collects minerals pass their hold state in, and no scene re-implements the mapping (the repo-wide parity guard is extended to enforce this).
- The inactivity-gap reset does not affect the pitch when the flag is ON (the pitch is derived from hold state alone); with the flag OFF the existing streak ladder and 1.5 s game-time reset behave exactly as today.
- Automated tests cover the pure mapping (base note at first mineral, top note at capacity, monotonic interior steps, capacity growth, degenerate capacities), the flag resolver (default ON, persisted OFF, corrupt/unavailable storage), and the dispatch in the game and gyms (fill-based pitch when ON, streak pitch when OFF); the full project test suite passes with the change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Impact

Players hear how full their hull is on every mineral pickup instead of how fast they are collecting: the first mineral of every hold sounds the same note and a full hull always sounds the same top note, so the approach to the next power-up is audible at a glance-free level.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The chime is a shared behaviour: the fill→pitch mapping and the flag gate must live in the shared core (`src/audio/mineralChime.ts` + the single `CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected()` dispatch) and be consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym that plays it (`GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, `GymLevel`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`, `GymPowerUpLeveling`). No divergent copies.
- **Cue assets are not re-baked.** `aihell-mineral-chime` (seed 32292) is reused; only the playback rate changes, so the ToneForge recipe, checksums and the ≤ 0.2 peak level guard stay untouched.
- **Musical ceiling.** A full hull must be a fixed, controlled note — never shrill — so the existing ladder ceiling (one octave) stays the maximum rate; the mapping is quantised onto the existing A-minor ladder rather than climbing without bound.
- **Game clock, not wall clock.** Any state the mapping keeps must be driven by the injected scene clock (`this.time.now`) so a paused scene can never change the cue.
- **No production UI toggles.** The flag resolver is build-agnostic (persisted value, default ON); any enable surface follows the existing dev-build-only rule in `src/core/featureFlags.ts`.
- **Scope creep.** Any further audio-feel ideas discovered during implementation (e.g. a distinct "hold about to fill" accent, per-capacity timbre) become separate work items, not scope here.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — pitch stagnates on large holds.** With capacities doubling to 40+, a seven-step ladder repeats a note for several pickups. *Mitigation:* the endpoints are what make the cue learnable (AC2/AC3); if the producer wants a per-pickup rise back, that is the continuous-rate alternative recorded in the Appendix, delivered as a follow-up item rather than scope here.
- **Risk — a pickup that fills the hold sounds the top note and immediately opens the choice overlay.** *Mitigation:* intended — the full-hull note is the audible confirmation that the power-up is due; the cue dispatch stays before the overlay opens.
- **Risk — chime dispatch order is behavioural, not cosmetic.** Playing before the credit would sound one step behind the HUD. *Mitigation:* AC2 pins the post-credit state, and the parity suite asserts one dispatch per pickup.
- **Risk — flag drift between the game and gyms.** *Mitigation:* one resolver in `src/core/featureFlags.ts`, one mapping function, one dispatch; the extended defines-once guard fails the build on a divergent copy.
- **Risk — doc guards go stale.** `mineralChime.docs.test.ts` asserts the current prose. *Mitigation:* the docs updates and the guard expectations are one AC, so a partial change fails the suite.
- **Assumption — quantised A-minor ladder with fixed endpoints** (first mineral = step 0, full hold = last step), rather than a continuous rate. *Rationale:* keeps both stated invariants for every capacity and preserves the documented musical rationale.
- **Assumption — "hull fullness" means the current run-scoped hold** (`store / capacity`), not cumulative run minerals.
- **Assumption — the pitch reflects the state after the pickup is credited**, and the inactivity-gap reset is inert while the flag is ON.

## Existing state

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — pure streak machine: `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]`, `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS = 1500`, `mineralChimeRate(step)`, `createMineralChime()` (`noteMineralCollected(nowMs)` / `reset()` / `step()`), a shared singleton plus `noteMineralCollected()`, `resetMineralChimeStreak()` and `mineralChimeStep()` (AH-0MWNMRCEW006N0EH).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playMineralCollectChimeSound(step = 0)` turns a ladder step into `{ rate: mineralChimeRate(step) }` on the baked `aihell-mineral-chime` cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — the single dispatch `noteMineralCollected()` (reads `this.time.now`, advances the streak, plays the chime); `resetMineralChimeStreak()` on run restart and scene teardown.
- Collection call sites currently play the chime **before** crediting the hold: `PlayScene._collectMineral`, `GymFormationScene._collectMineral`, `GymLevel._collectMineral`, `GymPowerUpsUtility._collectGymMineral`, `GymPowerUpLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping` (the last one already credits first).
- Hold state: `MineralHold` (`src/core/mineralHold.ts`) exposes `store`, `capacity`, `isFull`, `collect()`, `resolve()`; `GameState` mirrors it as `minerals` / `mineralCapacity`; each gym owns its own `MineralHold`-style model.
- Feature flags: `src/core/featureFlags.ts` holds one persisted record (`hangarWar`, default ON) under `ai_hell_feature_flags`, with a single resolver plus dev-build-only setters/toggles and corrupt-JSON/absent-storage fallbacks (AH-0MVZ0VGGQ0032KDP).
- Tests and guards: `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`, `src/audio/mineralChimeCue.test.ts`, `src/audio/mineralChime.docs.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts` (defines-once + every-call-site rules).
- Docs that describe the current streak behaviour (and must change): GDD §4.4.1 and the §7.3 cue table, `README.md` (hold + audio sections), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, and the `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` header comment.

## Desired change

- **Flag.** Add `hullFillMineralChime: true` to `FeatureFlagsRecord` / `DEFAULT_FEATURE_FLAGS`, load it with the same merge-over-defaults coercion as `hangarWar`, and expose a resolver (`resolveHullFillMineralChimeEnabled`) plus dev-build-only setter/toggle.
- **Pure mapping.** In `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`, add one pure function mapping a hold snapshot to a ladder step, e.g. `mineralChimeStepForFill(store, capacity)`:
  - first mineral of a hold (`store <= 1`) → step 0 (fixed base note);
  - a full hold (`store >= capacity`) → the ladder's last step (fixed top note);
  - interior fills spread monotonically over the interior steps, computed from the **credited** store and the current capacity, so capacity growth (5 → 10 → 20 → 40) keeps both fixed endpoints;
  - degenerate inputs (non-finite, `capacity <= 1`, negative store) clamp to a safe step instead of producing `NaN`.
  Keep the existing streak machine intact and selectable, so the flag-OFF path is unchanged.
- **Dispatch.** `CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected(fill)` takes the collecting scene's hold snapshot (`{ store, capacity }`), resolves the flag, and plays either the fill-based rate or the streak rate. The dispatch stays the only place that calls `playMineralCollectChimeSound`.
- **Call sites.** Move the chime after the hold credit in `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (so the filling pickup sounds the full-hull note) and pass the post-credit snapshot; `GymPowerUpLeveling` only needs to pass its snapshot.
- **Tests and docs.** Extend the pure-mapping, flag and parity suites; update `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4.1 and the §7.3 cue table), `README.md` (hold/mineral-chime prose), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, the `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-mineral-chime.yaml` header comment, and the doc-guard expectations in `src/audio/mineralChime.docs.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` — new pure `mineralChimeStepForFill(store, capacity)` mapping plus doc comments; keeps the streak machine for the flag-OFF path.
- `src/core/featureFlags.ts` — new persisted `hullFillMineralChime` flag (default ON), resolver and dev-only setter/toggle.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `noteMineralCollected(fill)` gains the hold snapshot and the flag gate.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — pass the post-credit hold snapshot; move the dispatch after the credit where it currently precedes it.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — unchanged rate→cue funnel (possibly a doc-comment update only).

No blocking producer questions were raised; the intake derived the brief from the work-item description, the existing chime implementation and the repo conventions. The decisions below are recorded so a reviewer can override them without re-deriving context.

Interior fills spread monotonically over the interior steps. Rationale: both stated invariants hold for every capacity, the cue stays musical (the documented reason the ladder is diatonic), and the rate ceiling keeps a full hull controlled rather than shrill. Alternative considered and not chosen: a continuous rate proportional to fill (rise of up to 12 semitones spread smoothly), which always rises per pickup but lands on non-scale pitches and no longer uses the kept ladder rationale. Source: `MINERAL_CHIME_RESET_GAP_MS` semantics in `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`.
- **Q: How is the feature flagged?** — Answer (Intake, from the work-item description and the existing flag precedent): a new persisted boolean in `src/core/featureFlags.ts` with the same storage key, merge-over-defaults load, corrupt-JSON fallback and dev-build-only enable surface as `hangarWar`, defaulting to ON. # Add occasional (40%) aggression level 1 hexes to ring 1

> Producer decisions recorded: **Q1 = A, Q2 = A, Q3 = A** (see the Appendix).
> This brief is final and ready for planning.

## Problem statement

Ring 1 is the opening ring, but only **one of its six hexes** (`hex-r1-2`) is
authored at aggression 1. The producer wants **occasional aggression-1 hexes**
to be a characteristic of ring 1 — roughly 40% of its hexes — so the opening
ring reads as a gentler on-ramp rather than a wall of aggression-2+/3 fights.

## Users

- **Player** — "The opening ring gives me a few genuinely easy footholds, so my
  first captures are achievable and I learn the loop before the harder tail."
- **Designer** — "Ring 1's aggression spread deliberately includes roughly 40%
  level-1 hexes, and the ring rules (one weapon hex as the strict maximum,
  retained gradient, ring-2-harder-than-ring-1) still hold."

## Existing state

- Ring 1 is authored (not yet procedural) in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`,
  mirrored by `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`. Current authored `baseAggression` for
  `hex-r1-1 … hex-r1-6`: **`2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`** — exactly one hex (16.7%) at
  aggression 1.
- `hex-r1-6` is the weapon hex (`waveLaser`) and the ring's strict maximum (6).
  `hex-r1-5` is the special mission (`hull-4`, `fortress` landmark); `hex-r1-4`
  carries the +60-salvage/+1-core contract.
- Aggression → difficulty mapping (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts`):
  `hexAggressionLevel(a) = MIN_LEVEL + a` (MIN_LEVEL = 1), so **aggression 1 →
  campaign level 2** (≈1.11× enemy count, boss HP ×1.06); aggression 0 →
  campaign level 1 (the identity level, 1.0×).
- The between-sortie tick adds a **capture-progress ramp**
  (`deploymentAggressionFor`) of +2 aggression across a ring's captures, so a
  ring-1 deployment still climbs as the ring is taken.
- **Ring 1's grind budget is currently `missed`**: `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors
  30–90 min (tolerance floor 24 min) and the shipped one-level model measures
  **23.7 min** (see `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` and
  `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`). Lowering hex aggression makes
  deployments easier/faster, so this trend continues (Q3 = accept, don't
  re-judge here).
- The current ring-1 band is **deliberately pinned** by
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` ("leaves ring 1's aggression band and
  recommended order untouched" expects `[2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6]`), so this change
  updates that pin by design.

## Desired change

Lower **`hex-r1-1` from aggression 2 to aggression 1**, giving ring 1 the band

**`hex-r1-1 … hex-r1-6` = `1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`**

so **2 of 6 hexes (33% ≈ 40%) sit at aggression 1** (campaign level 2). This is
the smallest edit that satisfies "occasional": it preserves the 3/4/6 gradient,
leaves the contract hex `hex-r1-4` (2) and the `fortress`+special-mission hex
`hex-r1-5` (4) untouched, and keeps `hex-r1-6` (6) as the strict maximum.

**Ring-rule preservation:**

- `hex-r1-6` stays the weapon hex and the strict maximum (6).
- The gradient survives (a hex at 3, one at 4, the weapon hex at 6).
- Ring 2 stays strictly harder than ring 1 (ring 1 floor stays 1, its max stays
  6 < ring 2's 8; ring 2 floor 2 > ring 1 floor 1).
- Grant uniqueness, one weapon hex, one special mission, and the landmark/
  contract placements are all unchanged.
- The `hexAggressionLevel(1) === 2` mapping is asserted so "aggression level 1"
  can never silently drift from its documented meaning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` ring-1 `baseAggression` values are **`1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`**
  for `hex-r1-1 … hex-r1-6`, and `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` mirrors them
  byte-for-value (CSV↔table parity test green).
- A new test in `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` pins that **2 of ring 1's
  6 hexes are at aggression 1** (`hex-r1-1`, `hex-r1-2`), that `hexAggressionLevel`
  resolves aggression 1 to campaign **level 2**, and that the gradient is
  retained (a hex at 3, one at 4 and the weapon hex `hex-r1-6` at 6 as the
  strict maximum).
- The ring-definition validation still holds: exactly one weapon hex per ring and
  it is ring 1's strict maximum, ring 2's floor stays above ring 1's floor and
  ring 2's maximum above ring 1's maximum, so `validateRingDefinitions(1, …)`
  reports ok.
- Consumers of the recommended/weakest-hex ordering (`hexIntel`'s
  `pickAttractHex`, `HexMapScene` default focus) are re-checked against the
  retuned data; any assertion changed carries a comment stating why the expected
  id is the one it is.
- **Data-only scope (Q3 = A):** the ring-timing *budget* is **not** re-judged
  here — no change to `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, the 30–90 min ring-1 window, its
  tolerance or the verdict logic — and the consequence stays recorded as a risk
  linked to **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X**.
- **Measured evidence re-measured and requoted (mechanical, not a re-judgement).**
  The ring-timing and one-level income artifacts are measured from the authored
  `baseAggression`, so regenerating them is unavoidable:
  `npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` and
  `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level --income-out
  docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`. With the regenerated artifacts the
  dependent pins and doc quotes are updated together, so
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchupDocs.test.ts`
  and `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` pass **without weakening a pin**
  (every changed expectation states why it changed). Ring 1's authored
  aggression-mass pins in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` move `18/19 →
  17/18`, and the before/after measured figures are recorded in a work-item
  comment.
- At least one testing/validation criterion is covered by the new assertions, and
  the changed-scope tests pass (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`,
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Ring 1 now opens with two genuinely easy aggression-1 footholds, so a new
player can bank their first captures before the ring's harder tail.

## Constraints

- **Authoring, not a new difficulty system.** Aggression → level stays
  `hexAggressionLevel` in `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts`; no parallel
  scaling path.
- **Data parity.** `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` and `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` are
  edited together; the parity test fails if they drift.
- **Ring rules are pinned by tests:** exactly one weapon hex and it is the strict
  maximum, unique ids/coordinates/grants, one special mission granting a hull, at
  most one landmark of each kind.
- **Whole-number aggression** in `[0, 9]`; the frontier budget/beatable-hex
  invariants are preserved.
- **Do not** re-word the ring-1 timing window or change `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`
  (Q3 = A; that is the budget chain's scope).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ring-timing consequence (accepted, Q3 = A).** Ring 1's grind is already below
  its tolerance floor (23.7 min vs a 24-min floor). Easier hexes will lower it
  further; the budget re-judgement is deliberately left to
  **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X**. Recorded, not re-worded.
- **Recommended-path reorder (confirmed by repo research).** Aggression orders
  the ring's recommended path, and `pickAttractHex` breaks equal-aggression ties
  by sorted id, so ring 1's attract/focus hex **moves from `hex-r1-2` to
  `hex-r1-1`** (both authored at aggression 1). Both consumers are pinned today
  and move with a stated reason, never silently re-pinned:
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` ("Ring 1's authored easiest hex … to be
  `hex-r1-2`") and `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` (the "ring 1's easiest (the
  default focus)" block asserts `hex:hex-r1-2`'s boss/grant/weaknesses in the
  panel — `hex-r1-1` is *the-dawnbreaker*, `hull-2`, weak to `nova|arc`).
- **Pinned measurement evidence (mechanical, unavoidable).** Both timing
  artifacts are measured from the authored aggression and are pinned literally:
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` (`23.7435` min ×2, the committed-artifact
  comparison, `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment ≈ 10.67`, the `42/23/17/30/15`
  unlock-pace pins, and a stale "`hex-r1-1` is aggression 2 → level 3" comment),
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchupDocs.test.ts` (requires `23.74 min` in
  `docs/BALANCING.md`) and `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` (quotes the
  artifact's ring-1/ring-2 means into `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`). The
  measurement must be regenerated and requoted or the suite cannot be green;
  the windows, targets and verdict logic stay untouched (Q3 = A). The ring-1
  grind verdict is expected to remain `missed` (it only gets shorter).
- **Hex income consequence.** Holding income is `10 × aggression`
  (`HEX_INCOME_MINERALS_PER_AGGRESSION`), so a fully held ring 1 pays **170**
  instead of **180** per tick and ring 1's authored aggression mass drops `18 →
  17`. The documented figures (`docs/Game Design Document.md`,
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`) are requoted; the income *rate* is not
  retuned (that is a separate balance knob).
- **Assumption:** "aggression level 1" means **aggression value 1 (campaign level
  2)**, confirmed by Q1 = A.
- **Assumption:** ring 1 stays authored (retiring the authored table is the
  separate blocked procedural-generation epic, AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA /
  AH-0MWLE72T500438E5), so this is a data edit, not a generator change.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Reworking ring 2, changing the timing window/budget, or
  adding a new difficulty system is out of scope; extra opportunities become
  linked work items.

## Key Files (verified by repo research)

**Data (the change itself)**

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — ring-1 `baseAggression` (`hex-r1-1` 2 → 1);
  runtime source of truth.
- `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` — the authored seed mirror (CSV↔table parity test
  fails if they drift).

**New assertions**

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` — update the pinned ring-1 band to
  `[1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6]` (`'leaves ring 1's aggression band and recommended order
  untouched'`, ~line 445) and add the "2 of 6 at aggression 1 / gradient
  retained / aggression 1 → campaign level 2" pins.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — the **unchanged** aggression → level
  mapping (`hexAggressionLevel`, `MIN_LEVEL = 1`); referenced by the new pins.

**Ordering consumers that reorder (confirmed, not conditional)**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — `'picks the weakest displayed unheld
  hex of the opening ring'` (~line 598) hard-pins `hex-r1-2`; the tie at
  aggression 1 now resolves to `hex-r1-1` (sorted-id tie-break).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts` — the default-focus / `SELECTED HEX` panel
  block (~line 474) keys off `hex:hex-r1-2` as "ring 1's easiest" and asserts its
  boss/grant/weaknesses; the default focus becomes `hex-r1-1`.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` — `'stays inside the ring-1 aggression-band
  budget'` (~line 268) pins ring 1's authored aggression mass `18` / `19` for the
  special hull; moves to `17` / `18`.

**Measured-evidence chain (regenerate, then requote)**

- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — regenerate with
  `npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`.
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — regenerate with
  `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level --income-out
  docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the ring-1 real-arena pins (`23.7435` mean,
  the committed-artifact comparisons, `mineralsPerCapturedDeployment ≈ 10.67`,
  unlock pace `42/23/17/30/15`) and the stale `hex-r1-1` aggression → level
  comment.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchupDocs.test.ts` — requires `23.74 min` in
  `docs/BALANCING.md`.
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — quotes the artifact's ring-1/ring-2
  grind + rush means into `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.

**Documentation requote**

- `docs/BALANCING.md` (ring-1 grind row), `docs/EVALUATION.md` (ring-timing
  table and prose), `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2 timing paragraphs and
  the `Σ aggression = 18` / `180`/tick income sentence, plus the hex-variety note
  that "no ring-1 row's `baseAggression` … changed"), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`
  (aggression-mass / income and ring-timing paragraphs), `README.md` (the outer-loop
  summary quoting 23.7 / 10.2 min).

## Related work

- **AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC** — Land ring 2's survivable aggression band (task,
  completed): the same authoring pattern applied to ring 2 (floor at aggression
  2, gradient retained). Closest precedent.
- **AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X** — Rebalance ring 1's grind budget (completed; re-rated
  to 23.7 min vs the 30–90 min window). Owns the ring-1 timing budget this change
  defers to (Q3 = A).
- **AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P** / **AH-0MWBBUAAT00340FS** — the aggression budget and
  redistribution rules (`ringAggressionBudget`, `beatableAggressionCeiling`,
  `deploymentAggressionFor`) that authored aggression must satisfy.
- **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic) and its child
  **AH-0MWLE72T500438E5** — Seeded procedural ring content generator (blocked):
  eventually must honour the same "occasional level-1 hex" proportion if the
  producer wants it generated behaviour rather than authored data.
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** — Author shipped hex variety content on ring 1
  (landmark/contract placement that must stay).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping completed item found (the closest,
  AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC, retunes ring 2, not ring 1).

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

### Q1 — What does "40% aggression level 1 hexes" mean on a 6-hex ring, and what is "level 1"?

Options presented: A) 2 of 6 hexes at aggression 1 (≈33% ≈ 40%; campaign level
2); B) 3 of 6 hexes at aggression 1 (50%); C) campaign level 1 = aggression 0
(identity difficulty) on 2–3 hexes. **Recommended: A.**

**Answer (producer, interactive reply): A** — **2 of 6 hexes at aggression 1**
(≈33% ≈ 40%), where "aggression level 1" means aggression value 1 → campaign
level 2.

### Q2 — Which ring-1 hexes get lowered to aggression 1?

Options presented: A) lower `hex-r1-1` 2 → 1, giving `1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`; B)
lower `hex-r1-3` 3 → 1, giving `2, 1, 1, 2, 4, 6`; C) producer specifies exact
ids/values. **Recommended: A.**

**Answer (producer, interactive reply): A** — lower **`hex-r1-1` 2 → 1**,
giving ring 1 the band **`1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`**.

### Q3 — How should the ring-1 grind-budget consequence be handled?

Options presented: A) data-only here; record the timing risk and leave the budget
re-judgement to AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X; B) re-measure and re-judge ring 1's budget
within this item. **Recommended: A.**

**Answer (producer, interactive reply): A** — **data-only**; record the timing
consequence as a risk and defer the budget re-judgement to
**AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X**. No `RING_TIMING_TARGETS` or window change here.

### Research notes (recorded, not questions)

- Current ring-1 band `[2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6]` and the pinned test read from
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` and `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`.
- Aggression→level mapping and multipliers read from
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` (`hexAggressionLevel`, `MIN_LEVEL = 1`).
- Ring-1 grind verdict read from `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` module comment and
  `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`.
- Ring-2 band precedent read from the completed AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC brief.
- Authored-table retirement is the blocked procedural-generation epic
  (AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA / AH-0MWLE72T500438E5), so this change is a data edit.
## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-25 — Plan session (auto-complete path: effort **Small**, risk **Low**,
  below the planning threshold). Six review stages run against the existing
  brief. Changes applied, all conservative and traceability-only:
  - **Key Files** corrected: the brief listed the ordering consumers as
    conditional ("if the recommended path reorders") — repo research confirms it
    does (`pickAttractHex` ties break by sorted id, so `hex-r1-1` displaces
    `hex-r1-2`) — and it omitted the whole measured-evidence chain
    (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json`,
    `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchupDocs.test.ts`,
    `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`) and
    `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`'s ring-1 aggression-mass pins.
  - **Acceptance Criteria** extended: the Q3 = A "data-only" criterion now
    distinguishes *budget re-judgement* (still out of scope) from the
    *mechanical re-measurement and requote* the pinned suite requires; the
    changed-scope test list names every affected file.
  - **Risks** extended with the pinned-measurement evidence and the hex-income
    consequence (`10 × aggression`, so a fully held ring 1 pays 170, not 180).
  - No change to the product decision (Q1/Q2/Q3 = A): `hex-r1-1` 2 → 1, ring 1 =
    `1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`, no timing-budget or window change.

## Appendix: plan review research notes (2026-11-25)

Recorded as research, not questions — each was answered from the repository and
no producer decision is implied.

- **The ring-1 band and its pin** — `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` and
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` author `2, 1, 3, 2, 4, 6`;
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts:449` pins that band.
- **The attract/focus hex moves** — `pickAttractHex`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts:1271`) sorts by aggression then **sorted id**,
  so a second aggression-1 hex makes `hex-r1-1` the ring's weakest target; both

  `HexMapScene.test.ts:474`) and move with a stated reason.
- **The timing measurement is aggression-driven and pinned literally** —
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` plays each hex at
  `hexDifficultyProfile(baseAggression).level` plus the ring's capture ramp, and
  `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` pins `23.7435` min, the committed artifact,
  the income pins (`10.67`, unlock pace `42/23/17/30/15`) and doc-derived means.
  Ring 1's authored aggression mass is also pinned (`18`/`19`) in
  `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts:268`.
- **Doc quotes are test-enforced** — `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchupDocs.test.ts:88`
  requires `23.74 min` in `docs/BALANCING.md`; `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts:736`
  quotes the artifact's four means into `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.
- **Agent assumption (recorded):** regenerating the artifacts and requoting their
  pins is a mechanical consequence of the data edit, **not** the budget
  re-judgement Q3 = A defers — windows, `RING_TIMING_TARGETS`, tolerances and the
  verdict logic are untouched, and the before/after figures are recorded for the
  budget owner. If the producer intended *no* measured-evidence movement at all,
  the change would have to be abandoned rather than split out, since the suite
  cannot be green otherwise.

# Add persisted `hullFillMineralChime` feature flag (default ON)

Part of AH-0MWW22HUZ008UWXT. The fill-based chime is gated behind a persisted flag so it ships ON and can be flipped OFF to restore today's streak ladder.

## Goal

Add a `hullFillMineralChime` boolean to the persisted feature-flag record, defaulting to **ON**, following the existing `hangarWar` precedent exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `FeatureFlagsRecord` gains `hullFillMineralChime: boolean`; `DEFAULT_FEATURE_FLAGS` sets it to `true`.
- `loadFeatureFlags()` merges the new field over defaults with the same boolean coercion (a corrupt/partial/absent record yields the default ON).
- `saveFeatureFlags()` persists it under the existing `ai_hell_feature_flags` key.
- A single resolver `resolveHullFillMineralChimeEnabled(flags = loadFeatureFlags())` returns `flags.hullFillMineralChime === true`.
- Dev-build-only `setHullFillMineralChimeEnabled(enabled, env)` and `toggleHullFillMineralChimeEnabled(env)`, matching the `hangarWar` guards (no-op outside dev build).
- `src/core/featureFlags.test.ts` covers: default ON; persisted OFF round-trips; corrupt JSON → default ON; absent storage → default ON; non-boolean value → default ON; setter/toggle are no-ops outside a dev build and persist inside one.
- `npm run build` (typecheck) passes.

## Key Files

- `src/core/featureFlags.ts`
- `src/core/featureFlags.test.ts`

## Constraints

- Same storage key, same merge-over-defaults coercion, same SSR-safe/corrupt fallbacks as `hangarWar`.
- No production UI toggle (dev-build-only enable surface, per `isDevBuild`).
- Do not change the `hangarWar` behaviour.

## Existing state

`src/core/featureFlags.ts` already implements the `hangarWar` precedent (record, defaults, load/save/reset, resolver, dev-only setter/toggle). Extend it; do not fork a second flag store.

# Add pure `mineralChimeStepForFill(store, capacity)` mapping

Part of AH-0MWW22HUZ008UWXT. The fill→pitch mapping must exist once as a pure, unit-tested function so the game and every gym consume the same rule.

## Goal

Add a pure function to `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` that maps the post-credit hold state to a ladder step with fixed endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New exported pure function `mineralChimeStepForFill(store: number, capacity: number): number` in `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` (no Phaser, no clock, no side effects).
- **First mineral** (`store <= 1`) → step 0 (fixed base note).
- **Full hold** (`store >= capacity`) → `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES.length - 1` (fixed top note).
- **Interior fills** spread monotonically over the interior steps, computed from the credited `store` and current `capacity`; the mapping never falls as `store` grows within one capacity.
- **Capacity growth** keeps both endpoints: for capacities 5, 10, 20, 40 the first mineral is step 0 and the full hold is the top step.
- **Degenerate inputs** clamp to a safe step rather than `NaN`: non-finite store/capacity, `capacity <= 1`, negative store. A full/degenerate hold still yields the top step; a first/negative store yields step 0.
- A red deposit (`MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE` = 10) jumps the equivalent number of steps in one pickup (since the function reads the credited store).
- Unit tests in `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts` cover every rule above, computing expected rates from the exported ladder (not a copied number).
- The existing streak machine (`createMineralChime`, `mineralChimeRate`, gap reset) is unchanged and still exported.
- `npm run build` passes.

## Design note (from intake, override-able)

Quantise onto the existing A-minor ladder `[0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10]` with fixed endpoints — `store<=1` → 0, `store>=capacity` → last — rather than a continuous rate. Interior spread: `round((store - 1) / (capacity - 1) * (last))`, clamped into `[0, last]`. This keeps both learnability invariants for every capacity and preserves the one-octave musical ceiling. The streak ladder stays selectable for the flag-OFF path.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/mineralChime.ts`
- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`

## Constraints

- Cue asset untouched; only playback rate derived.
- Mapping must be quantised onto the existing ladder — never climb unbounded.
- One implementation only; the parity guard will be extended to enforce it (a later child).

## Existing state

`src/audio/mineralChime.ts` holds `MINERAL_CHIME_SEMITONES`, `mineralChimeRate(step)` and the streak machine. `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE` lives in `src/core/rules.ts` (10).
data.title: Add pure mineralChimeStepForFill(store, capacity) mapping

# Gate the chime dispatch on the flag and take a hold snapshot

Part of AH-0MWW22HUZ008UWXT. The single shared dispatch `CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected()` must resolve the flag and choose the fill-based rate or the legacy streak rate.

## Goal

Change `CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected()` to accept the collecting scene's post-credit hold snapshot `{ store, capacity }`, resolve `resolveHullFillMineralChimeEnabled()`, and play either `mineralChimeStepForFill(store, capacity)` or the legacy streak step.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the flag child (AH-0MWW36R7W006DGUZ) and the mapping child (AH-0MWW36WT3003LYKL).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `noteMineralCollected(fill: { store: number; capacity: number })` resolves the flag once per call.
- **Flag ON** → play `playMineralCollectChimeSound(mineralChimeStepForFill(fill.store, fill.capacity))`; the streak machine and its gap reset are **not advanced** on this path (the pitch is derived from hold state alone).
- **Flag OFF** → the existing behaviour is unchanged: advance the shared streak with `this.time.now` and play `mineralChimeStep()`.
- `noteMineralCollected` remains the **only** place that calls `playMineralCollectChimeSound` (the parity guard already enforces this).
- The module doc block on the method is updated to describe the flag gate, the hold snapshot and the two paths, and to state the pitch is post-credit.
- The dispatch still reads the scene clock only on the flag-OFF path; the flag-ON path derives nothing from wall clock or scene clock.
- `npm run build` passes.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — the single dispatch (+ imports of the resolver and mapping).

## Constraints

- Gym↔game parity: this stays the one shared dispatch consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; no scene re-implements the gate or the mapping.
- Playing before the credit would sound one step behind the HUD — the post-credit snapshot is the contract (call-site reorder is a separate child).
- No change to the baked cue or `playMineralCollectChimeSound`.

## Existing state

`CombatCoreScene.noteMineralCollected()` currently calls `advanceMineralChime(this.time.now)` then `playMineralCollectChimeSound(mineralChimeStep())`. `resetMineralChimeStreak()` is called on run restart and scene teardown (both remain, harmless on the flag-ON path).

# Pass post-credit hold state at every chime call site

Part of AH-0MWW22HUZ008UWXT. Every collection path must credit the hold first, then dispatch the chime with the post-credit snapshot, so the filling pickup sounds the full-hull note.

## Goal

Update the five player-pickup call sites to pass their hold snapshot to `noteMineralCollected(fill)` and, at the four that currently play before crediting, move the dispatch **after** the credit.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the dispatch child (AH-0MWW3725H001KFW3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayScene._collectMineral`: move `noteMineralCollected({ store: gameState.minerals, capacity: gameState.mineralCapacity })` **after** `gameState.addMinerals(mineral.value)` (and the pickup-credit step), so the snapshot is post-credit.
- `GymFormationScene._collectMineral`: move the dispatch after `mineralHoldModel.collect(mineral.value)` and pass `{ store: mineralHoldModel.store, capacity: mineralHoldModel.capacity }`.
- `GymLevel._collectMineral`: move the dispatch after `mineralHold.collect(mineral.value)` (and before/after `_resolveMineralHold()` as appropriate to reflect the *credited* store) and pass the snapshot. Ensure the full-hull note still sounds on the filling pickup.
- `GymPowerUpsUtility._collectGymMineral`: move the dispatch after `mineralHold.collect(mineral.value)` and pass the snapshot.
- `GymPowerUpLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping`: already credits first; pass `{ store: hold.store, capacity: hold.capacity }` (no reorder).
- `GymWeaponLeveling._collectMineralsOverlapping`: already credits first; pass the snapshot (same shared dispatch).
- No call site passes a pre-credit snapshot, and no call site re-implements the mapping or the flag gate.
- Existing parity test `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts` still passes (one dispatch per pickup), extended in a later child for the new signature.
- `npm run build` passes and the changed-scope test gate passes.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`

## Constraints

- Dispatch stays **after** credit everywhere so the full-hull pickup sounds the top note (intake answer: post-credit).
- The dispatch must stay before the hold-full choice overlay opens, so the audible confirmation precedes the pause.
- No divergent copies — all sites call the one shared dispatch.

## Existing state

Currently: PlayScene, GymFormationScene, GymLevel, GymPowerUpsUtility play the chime **before** crediting; GymPowerUpLeveling and GymWeaponLeveling already credit first.

# Extend the chime test suites and the repo-wide parity guard

Part of AH-0MWW22HUZ008UWXT. The pure mapping, the flag and the dispatch must be pinned by automated tests, and the defines-once guard extended so a divergent copy fails the build.

## Goal

Extend the existing suites so the fill-based behaviour, the flag gate and the single-source rule are all enforced.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the call-site child (AH-0MWW377CQ001QWQI) and the flag child (AH-0MWW36R7W006DGUZ).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pure mapping** (`src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`): base note at the first mineral, top note at capacity, monotonic interior steps, capacity growth (5/10/20/40) keeps both endpoints, red-deposit jump, degenerate capacities (non-finite, `capacity <= 1`, negative store) clamp safely, resolving a hold returns the next pickup to base (store 0/1 → step 0).
- **Flag resolver** (`src/core/featureFlags.test.ts`): covered by the flag child; the dispatch tests additionally assert default ON and persisted OFF paths.
- **Dispatch in the game and gyms** (`src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts`): with the flag ON a pickup plays the fill-based step (`playMineralCollectChimeSound` receives the `mineralChimeStepForFill` value for the post-credit hold), the first mineral sounds step 0 and a filling pickup sounds the top step; with the flag OFF the streak pitch is played (existing behaviour). Cover `PlayScene` and at least one formation gym plus the bespoke gyms. Keep the existing "exactly one chime per pickup", enemy-silence, reset and voice-limiter cases passing.
- **Defines-once guard extension**: the repo-wide guard asserts `mineralChimeStepForFill` is defined only in `src/audio/mineralChime.ts` and that no scene defines its own fill→pitch copy; the flag resolver `resolveHullFillMineralChimeEnabled` is imported only by the shared core (and its own module/tests). Fails the build on a divergent copy.
- The full project test suite passes via the test skill (`/skill:test`), not ad-hoc `pytest`/`vitest`.

## Key Files

- `src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts`
- `src/core/featureFlags.test.ts` (extends the flag child's cases)

## Constraints

- Tests serve a meaningful purpose (each pins a stated AC), no assertion weakening.
- Never invoke test commands directly — use the test skill.
- Do not re-implement the mapping in a test helper; compute expectations from the exported function/ladder.

## Existing state

`src/audio/mineralChime.test.ts`, `src/audio/mineralChimeCue.test.ts`, `src/audio/mineralChime.docs.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/mineralChime.parity.test.ts` (defines-once + every-call-site rules) already exist; extend rather than replace.
