# Randomize the hex war starter weapon

## Problem statement

The Hangar War ("hex war") fleet always begins a war with the same free
starter weapon — the Spread Cannon (`spread`, `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`), authored in
the hangar catalogue as the `starter: true` entry and seeded into every fresh
payload's `unlockedWeapons`. The first battle therefore always flies the same
gun. The producer wants the starter weapon randomised from the ring-1 weapons
in the catalogue, free and auto-equipped for the very first battle.

## Users

- **The returning hangar-war player** — "A fresh war should feel like a
  different starting hand, not the same Spread Cannon every reset."
- **The first-time hangar-war player** — "The very first battle should start me
  with one of the catalogue's weapons, already fitted, at no cost."
- **The maintainer** — "The draw must be deterministic for the war seed and
  must never let the player lose the starter (no soft-lock)."

User stories:

- As a player, when I start a new war (or restart one), I want the very first
  battle to be equipped with a randomly chosen ring-1 weapon at no cost, so
  each war opens with a different kit.
- As a player, I want the randomised starter to remain owned and free through
  that war, including after a battle I flew it in, so I can never be left with
  no weapon.
- As a player with an existing save, I want my current starter and loadout left
  exactly as they are, so the change does not rewrite my war.

## Acceptance Criteria

> Answers recorded from the producer on 2026-11-25 (Appendix Q1–Q3): the
> randomised thing is **the weapon available in the very first battle, at no
> cost**; the draw pool is **all ring-1 weapons**, and the drawn weapon is
> **free**; the starter is **auto-equipped**.

- A **fresh war** (`createDefaultPayload(<seed>)` or a first load with no save)
  draws one starter from **every purchasable ring-1 weapon** in the hangar
  catalogue (`kind === 'weapon'`, `minRing <= 1`, `isPurchasableEntry`) and
  **auto-equips** it in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, so the very first
  deployment (`buildHangarDeployment`) carries it as a starting weapon. The draw
  is **deterministic for the payload seed** (the same seed always yields the
  same starter; different seeds can yield different starters, and a seeded
  sweep shows every eligible entry is reachable). The drawn starter costs
  nothing — no minerals or cores are deducted, even when its catalogue price is
  non-zero.
- A **restart** (`restartHangarWar`, which supplies a fresh random seed)
  re-draws the starter with that fresh seed and auto-equips it, while still
  preserving `bestScore` and saved builds and returning the rest of the hangar
  to its documented starting kit (zero salvage, ring 1, no queued attacks).
- The randomised starter is **owned and free for that war**, is never
  consumed by `consumeDeployedShip` on **win or loss**, and is protected
  exactly as today's `spread` starter is — so no battle outcome can leave the
  fleet without a free weapon (no soft-lock). Its permanent level rows follow
  the existing starter rules.
- **Existing saves are unchanged**: a stored payload keeps its current owned
  starter, loadout and hangar state (no re-roll on load, no loadout rewrite, no
  back-fill). Migration stays field-presence based, no schema version bump is
  required, and a legacy save's implicit starter remains `spread`; a legacy
  save's empty loadout is still filled by the existing hangar auto-fit on open,
  not by this change.
- Regression coverage is added/updated for: seeded determinism and ring-1
  eligibility, the auto-equipped first deployment, no-cost acquisition, starter
  survival through win **and** loss consumption, a legacy-save round-trip with
  no re-roll, the restart re-draw, the attract/traversal bot invariance and the
  `GymHexWar`/`GymHangar` parity path — with the existing pinned expectations
  that hard-code `spread` as the starter updated deliberately (red-first where
  the behaviour changes).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically
  the GDD's Hangar War starting-kit, empty-loadout and auto-fit sections (the
  documented "starter never auto-equips" rule is superseded for a fresh war's
  first deployment), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` wherever the starter appears, and the
  affected module docblocks.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The very first Hangar War battle now flies a randomly chosen ring-1 weapon at
no cost — seeded per war and already auto-equipped — instead of always the
Spread Cannon, while an existing save keeps the starter and loadout it already
has.

## Constraints

- **Draw pool.** Every purchasable ring-1 weapon entry in the hangar catalogue,
  including `spread` itself; grant-only entries (`GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`) and
  non-weapon kinds are excluded. The draw iterates the catalogue, never a
  hard-coded four, so AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 grows the pool without another
  change.
- **Auto-equip supersedes AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D for a fresh war only.** The
  initial loadout is no longer empty for a new war; the post-battle reset still
  empties the loadout and the hangar auto-fit still fills an empty one, and an
  existing save's loadout is never rewritten. The GDD's empty-loadout and
  starter-never-auto-equips notes must be updated accordingly.
- **No cost.** The draw must not deduct minerals or cores; a drawn paid weapon
  is free only as the war's starter, and its normal price and ring gate remain
  for any future purchase.
- **No soft-lock.** The war's starter must be owned and protected from
  `consumeDeployedShip` on win and loss (the protection must key off the war's
  starter id, not the fixed `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`).
- **Determinism.** Randomness must come from the existing seeded hangar-war RNG
  (`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`) derived from the war seed — no unseeded
  `Math.random()` — so replays, traversal tests and the parity harness stay
  deterministic.
- **Attract/traversal bot invariance.** If the unpicked default `spread`
  becomes an unowned zero-price entry, the bot's cheapest-useful-unlock rule
  must not start buying it: keep its decisions, seeded replays and pinned
  unlock pace byte-identical (e.g. exclude zero-price entries from the bot's
  candidate gate, a no-op today) and prove it with the existing traversal
  tests.
- **Migration.** The versioned payload's field-presence policy holds: an
  additive per-war starter field (or an equivalent seed-derived record), no
  schema bump, and old saves keep `spread`.
- Balance is otherwise untouched: no drawn ring-2/gated weapon, no change to
  salvage, prices or the ring model.
- CHANGELOG.md is handled by the ship/release pipeline — do not edit it.

## Existing state

- `STARTER_WEAPON_ID = 'spread'` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) and the
  catalogue entry `{ id: 'spread', starter: true, price: { minerals: 0, cores: 0 } }`
  designate the one free starter weapon.
- `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID = 'spread'` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`)
  seeds `createDefaultPayload(...).hangar.unlockedWeapons`, and the fresh
  payload's `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` is empty.
- `ownsEntry` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) returns true for every
  `entry.starter`, so `spread` is owned regardless of the payload's sets.
- `consumeDeployedShip` protects `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` and resets the active
  loadout to empty after every hex battle.
- `restartHangarWar` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) builds a fresh
  payload from a fresh random seed (`randomSeed()`), preserving `bestScore` and
  saved builds.
- The hangar auto-fit (`isDefaultHangarLoadout` / boss-aware suggestion) fills
  an empty loadout on open, so today the owned starter is what a first war
  flies after the screen is opened; a deployment without opening the hangar
  carries only the permanent cannon.
- `HANGAR_FALLBACK_WEAPON_ID = STARTER_WEAPON_ID` is the hangar screen's
  fallback pointer.
- The catalogue's weapon list is currently four entries (`spread`,
  `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster`), all `minRing: 1`; AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91
  will derive one entry per `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` weapon, so the pool grows.
- The attract/traversal bot's `cheapestUsefulUnlock` (pure economy) and
  `cheapestSeededUnlock` (`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) both gate through
  `isBotPurchaseCandidate`; today `spread` is starter-owned, so its zero price
  never enters the comparison.
- `hangarEconomy.test.ts` pins `STARTER_WEAPON_ID === DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`;
  several store, screen, gym and integration suites hard-code `spread` as the
  starter.

## Desired change

A fresh war draws its starter from every purchasable ring-1 weapon in the
hangar catalogue using the war's seeded hangar-war RNG, records it as the war's
starter, owns it at no cost and auto-equips it in the initial loadout so the
very first deployment flies it. The starter is protected from win/loss
consumption; restarting re-draws with the fresh seed; existing saves keep their
current starter and loadout. The catalogue's fixed `starter: true` ownership is
replaced by the per-war starter (with `spread` as the legacy fallback for old
saves), the attract bot's candidate rule is kept unchanged, and the GDD and
parity docs are updated.

**Key Files:**

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `STARTER_WEAPON_ID`, the `starter: true`
  weapon entry and the ring-1 weapon list: the starter designation becomes
  per-war (or the weapon list is exposed as the draw pool).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `DEFAULT_STARTING_WEAPON_ID`,
  `createDefaultPayload` (draw, record and auto-equip the starter), `parseHangar`
  (legacy saves keep `spread`; additive field if used).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `ownsEntry` (starter ownership),
  `consumeDeployedShip` (protect the war's starter),
  `resolveActiveLoadout`/`ownedEntriesOf`, and the bot's candidate gate.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — the seeded `pick` used for the draw.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `restartHangarWar` re-draw,
  `HANGAR_FALLBACK_WEAPON_ID`, and the FREE/owned unlock row.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — deployment resolution and the
  auto-fit consumers.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` — the traversal bot's shared candidate gate
  (invariance guard).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar*.test.ts` — pinned `spread` starter expectations.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§ Hangar War starting kit / empty-loadout /
  auto-fit) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the starter rule.

## Risks and mitigations

- **A free drawn ring-gated weapon undermines the unlock tree** → the pool is
  ring-1 purchasable weapons only; free only as that war's starter; its normal
  price and ring gate remain for purchase.
- **Soft-lock if the starter is consumed** → the war's starter is owned and
  protected in `consumeDeployedShip`; no battle outcome removes it.
- **The bot starts buying the now-unowned zero-price `spread`** → the shared
  `isBotPurchaseCandidate` gate must exclude zero-price entries (a no-op today)
  or the traversal/unlock-pace tests must prove the decision stream unchanged.
- **Non-determinism breaks replays and parity** → seeded draw through
  `createHangarWarRng`; a same-seed test plus the gym parity suites cover it.
- **Auto-equip contradicts a documented rule** → the GDD and the
  AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D note are updated in the same change; legacy saves are
  explicitly not rewritten.
- **Scope creep into the catalogue-derivation item** → AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91
  stays separate; this change iterates whatever the catalogue holds.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons
  in the loadout (default weapon only): the empty-loadout default this change
  supersedes for a fresh war's first deployment, and the rule it must preserve
  for legacy saves.
- **AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91** — Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon
  entries from weapons.csv: grows the catalogue's ring-1 weapon list, which is
  the random draw pool.
- **AH-0MWW5RACR000UCKU** — Maintain weapon Lvl between losses: touches
  `consumeDeployedShip`, whose starter protection this change must respect.
- **AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3** — Hangar War needs a restart button: the restart
  already supplies a fresh random seed, which makes the per-restart re-draw
  natural.
- **AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD** — Automatically select strong weapons: the
  empty-loadout auto-fit that remains the path for a legacy save's empty
  loadout.
- **AH-0MWLE90B30013MPZ** — War reset preserves saved builds: the reset
  contract the re-draw must not disturb.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — Candidate D (Hangar War) design of record;
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar War.

## Assumptions (documented, reversible)

- **A1 — routine:** "the catalogue" is the hangar catalogue (`HANGAR_CATALOGUE`),
  the one authored weapon list the game consumes; the full `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`
  is reached through it (AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91).
- **A2 — routine:** the draw is per **war**, not per deployment — the war seed
  identifies a fresh war and `restartHangarWar` re-seeds — so no per-battle
  randomness or new persisted state is needed.
- **A3 — routine:** existing saves are not rewritten — no re-roll on load and
  no back-fill; they keep whatever starter and loadout they own today.
- **A4 — routine:** the draw is seeded through `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`, so
  the same seed always yields the same starter (replay and parity tests).
- **A5 — producer answers (2026-11-25):** Q1 = the weapon available in the very
  first battle at no cost; Q2 = all ring-1 weapons, free; Q3 = auto-equip.
  These are the design of record for this item.
- **A6 — routine:** the drawn starter is recorded on the hangar (e.g. an
  additive per-war `starterWeaponId`, or an equivalent seed-derived record) and
  owned for that war; `spread` remains the legacy fallback for a save that
  predates the field. Planning chooses the exact record.
- **A7 — routine:** the draw pool includes `spread` itself (it is a purchasable
  ring-1 weapon), so a fresh war can still start with the Spread Cannon by
  chance; "randomised" does not mean "never spread".
- **A8 — routine:** after a battle the existing reset and hangar auto-fit rules
  apply; only the fresh war's initial loadout is auto-equipped by this change.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Which "starter weapon" is being randomised? (answered)

The item's wording could mean two different things:

- (a) the **free starter weapon the fleet owns** from its first deployment —
  today `spread` (Spread Cannon), owned but not equipped; or
- (b) the **weapon a hex deployment actually flies** — today an empty default
  loadout resolves to the ship's permanent cannon, and the hangar's auto-fit is
  the only thing that fills it.

**Recommended:** (a) — it is the only fixed "starter weapon" in the Hangar
War, matches the catalogue's `starter: true` entry, and (b) would contradict
the documented empty-loadout rule AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "The weapon that is available in the very
first battle, at no cost." — the randomised starter is the weapon the **first
battle** carries, drawn free; combined with Q3 it is auto-equipped. Source:
interactive reply.

### Q2 — Which weapons are eligible, and is the drawn starter free? (answered)

- (a) every weapon entry in the hangar catalogue, free for that war;
- (b) only weapons reachable at ring 1 / already unlockable, free;
- (c) every catalogue weapon, but at its normal price (the "starter" is only
  the owned entry, not a free one).

**Recommended:** (a) — "available weapons in the catalogue" reads as the full
weapon list, and "starter" implies free; ring gating still governs purchase, so
a drawn ring-2 weapon is free as the starter but not buyable.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "all ring 1, and yes, free" — the draw pool
is every ring-1 purchasable weapon, and the drawn starter costs nothing.
Source: interactive reply.

### Q3 — Should the randomised starter be equipped for the first deployment? (answered)

- (a) no — keep the documented "starter never auto-equips" rule; the starter
  stays owned and the hangar's auto-fit puts it into the first run;
- (b) yes — a fresh war's `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` starts with the drawn
  starter so the first deployment flies it immediately.

**Recommended:** (a) — preserves AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D and the
starter-never-auto-equips rule; (b) changes a documented producer decision.

**Answer (producer, 2026-11-25):** "auto-equip" — the fresh war's initial
loadout carries the drawn starter so the first deployment flies it. Source:
interactive reply. This supersedes the empty-loadout default and the
starter-never-auto-equips rule **for a fresh war only**; legacy saves are not
rewritten.

### R1 — Duplicate check (routine, answered)

No completed item already satisfies this request. Closest completed work is
AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with no extra weapons — the default
loadout), AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD (auto-fit strong weapons) and AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3
(restart with a fresh seed); none randomises the starter weapon.
AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 is related future work (grows the weapon pool), not a
duplicate. Source: `wl search "hex war starter weapon"`, `wl search "random
starter"`, `wl search "starting weapon catalogue"`.

### R2 — Randomness source (routine, answered)

The war already carries a seeded stream (`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`,
`createHangarWarRng(seed)` with `pick`), derived from the payload's seed, and
`restartHangarWar` supplies a fresh `randomSeed()`. Using it keeps every
replay, traversal and parity harness deterministic. Research: inspected
`src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`
(`restartHangarWar`), `src/core/rng.ts`.

### R3 — Migration policy (routine, answered)

The versioned hangar-war payload migrates by field presence; old saves must
keep their current starter. `parseHangar` does not force a starter weapon into
`unlockedWeapons` today (only the hull is forced), so an old save's owned
starter is whatever it stored. Research: inspected `parseHangar` in
`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` and `docs/Game Design Document.md`
§ `ai_hell_hangar_war`.

### R4 — Attract-bot impact (routine, answered)

If `spread` stops being starter-owned, its zero-price entry would become the
bot's cheapest useful unlock and change the seeded traversal/unlock pace
(pinned by the AH-0MWKT12BT001106T tests). The shared `isBotPurchaseCandidate`
gate is the one place both bot consumers read; excluding zero-price entries
there is a no-op today (the only free entry is starter-owned) and keeps the
demo unchanged. Research: inspected `cheapestUsefulUnlock`
(`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`), `cheapestSeededUnlock`
(`src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts`) and `isBotPurchaseCandidate`
(`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** – Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (default weapon only) (completed)
- **AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG** – Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (completed)
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** – Make weapons both cumalative and time out (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvzj6v1j001da9d, 0mw8f7nh1002pqe3, 0mworojyt004wpsd, acceptance, active (+391 more)
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, active, actually, added, additive (+362 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: acceptance, active, actually, added, additive (+306 more)

## Plan (features and implementation tasks)

Phasing: one tracer bullet cut into vertical slices — every child lands code,
tests and the docblock it touches together, so the tree is never left half
wired. The item is Small (~19 h recommended), so no horizontal phases; the
children are executed in the dependency order below.

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AH-0MWWM4YSH00078CI — Test: randomised starter weapon contract (test-first) | task | — | AC1 (pool + determinism), AC5 (red-first contract) |
| 2 | AH-0MWWM4ZQE0069NB5 — Per-war starter draw, ownership and free auto-equip | feature | 1 | AC1 (draw, auto-equip, no cost), AC3 (owned), AC4 (migration) |
| 3 | AH-0MWWM50OD001K3V9 — Starter survives battle-end consumption | feature | 2 | AC3 (win and loss) |
| 4 | AH-0MWWM51N6002BWL0 — Restart re-draw and legacy-save preservation | feature | 2 | AC2 (restart), AC4 (no re-roll/back-fill) |
| 5 | AH-0MWWM52JI008KJCK — Attract-bot invariance for the free starter | task | 2 | AC5 (bot/traversal + unlock pace) |
| 6 | AH-0MWWM53FN005Z4XM — Repin spread starter expectations and verify parity | task | 2, 3, 4, 5 | AC5 (pins, first deployment, gym parity), AC7 (full suite) |
| 7 | AH-0MWWM54FN0070XC4 — Document the randomised starter weapon | docs | 6 | AC6 (GDD, GYM_PARITY, docblocks, README) |

### Agreed contract (implementation must follow; child 1 pins it)

- New pure module `src/core/hangarWar/starterWeapon.ts` exporting
  `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)`, `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)` and
  `resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar, catalogue?)`.
  - Pool = `kind === 'weapon'` && `minRing <= 1` && `isPurchasableEntry(entry)`;
    iterates the catalogue, so AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 grows it with no change here.
  - Draw = `createHangarWarRng(seed).pick(pool)` — no `Math.random()`.
  - Resolve = `hangar.starterWeaponId` when present, else the legacy
    `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` (`spread`); a corrupt/unknown id falls back to the legacy
    constant (never throws).
- `HangarState.starterWeaponId?: string` — additive optional, migrated by field
  presence exactly like `unlockedPowerUps`/`weaponLevels`: absent stays absent on
  parse (legacy save resolves to `spread`), no schema version bump, and a fresh
  payload always writes it.
- Fresh payload (`createDefaultPayload(seed)`): `hangar.starterWeaponId` = the
  draw, `hangar.unlockedWeapons = [drawnId]`, `hangar.activeLoadout.startingWeapons
  = [drawnId]`, balances `0` (the draw spends nothing).
- Catalogue: `starter: true` is retired from the `spread` weapon entry (only
  `hull-1` keeps it); `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` survives re-documented as the **legacy
  fallback** constant to avoid rename churn.
- Ownership: `ownsEntry` also returns true for
  `entry.id === resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar)`, so a corrupt save can never lose
  the war's starter.
- Consumption: `consumeDeployedShip` protects `resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar)`
  (not the fixed constant) and still resets `activeHull`/`activeLoadout` to the
  starter kit, so the post-battle auto-fit rule (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D) is intact.
- Display: the hangar screen's `FREE` row label keys off the war's starter (or a
  zero price), never `entry.starter`; the bot and unlock-pace exclusions live in
  the shared helpers (`isBotPurchaseCandidate`, `deriveUnlockPace`), never in a
  scene.
- Legacy: `parseHangar` never synthesises `starterWeaponId`, never re-rolls and
  never rewrites `unlockedWeapons`/`activeLoadout`.

### Open questions

None. The producer decisions were answered at intake (Appendix Q1–Q3); planning
added only the routine decisions D1–D7 below, none of which needs producer
input.

## Appendix addendum — planning routine decisions (2026-11-25)

### D1 — Per-war record shape (routine, answered by planning)

**Question:** is the drawn starter persisted as a new hangar field or re-derived
from the seed on every load? **Answer:** an additive optional
`hangar.starterWeaponId`, presence-migrated exactly like
`unlockedPowerUps`/`weaponLevels` (absent → legacy `spread`, no schema bump,
never synthesised on parse). Chosen over a seed-derived re-draw on load because a
catalogue change must not silently re-roll a live war. Research: inspected
`parseHangar`/`createDefaultPayload` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) and
the additive-field migration notes in the store's module docblock.

### D2 — Catalogue `starter` reclassification (routine)

`starter: true` is retired from the `spread` weapon entry (only `hull-1` keeps
it) and starter ownership moves to `resolveStarterWeaponId`; the consequence is
that the `FREE` row label (`hangarScreen.ts:797`) and the unlock-pace exclusion
must key off the war's starter / zero price rather than `entry.starter`. Owned by
child 2 (ownership + label) and child 5 (report + bot).

### D3 — Bot and report guard (routine)

The zero-price exclusion lands in the shared `isBotPurchaseCandidate` gate with
`deriveUnlockPace`'s starter/free exclusion re-keyed equivalently; both are
no-ops for today's catalogue, proven by the existing traversal and ring-timing
suites plus one new test.

### D4 — Restart needs no new code path (routine)

`restartHangarWar` already rebuilds from `createDefaultPayload(freshSeed)`, so
the re-draw follows from child 2. Child 4 pins it, the preserved
`bestScore`/saved-builds contract and the legacy no-re-roll round-trip.

### D5 — Test-first scope (routine)

The red-first contract item (child 1) pins the agreed API names so the
implementation children cannot drift; it contains no production change.

### D6 — Gym parity (routine)

No gym-local change is expected: `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` consume the shipped
hangar, deployment and capture code, so the drawn starter reaches them through
the shared core. Child 6 verifies it and updates the pinned expectations.

### D7 — Suite gate (routine)

The full suite is enforced by the dev-push gate and run through the test skill
(`/skill:test`); child 6 records the green run. No ad-hoc full-suite invocations.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-25 — plan session: created 7 children (1 test-first task, 3 features,
  2 guard/verification tasks, 1 docs item), wired the dependency DAG
  (1 → 2 → {3, 4, 5} → 6 → 7), recorded routine decisions D1–D7, no open
  questions.

# Bug: Ring-2's modifier grants have no hangar catalogue entry

Discovered-from: AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91 (deliberately out of scope there — same class of drift, different fix).

## Summary
`hex-r2-8` grants `armour-plating`, `hex-r2-9` grants `systems-upgrade` and `hex-r2-10` grants `firepower-up` (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`). `resolveHexGrant` falls through to its final `kind: 'modifier'` default (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:320`), so each id lands in `hangar.ownedModifiers` with **no catalogue entry**. Consequences:

- invisible in `buildHangarUnlockRows` (catalogue-driven);
- dropped by `resolveActiveLoadout` → `ownedEntriesOf`, so never equippable;
- **no `ModifierEffect`**, so the grant has no observable effect on any deployment.

Three of ring 2's twelve hexes therefore pay out a reward that cannot be seen, equipped or felt.

## The design question that must be settled first
The three ids map **exactly** onto `HullUpgrades { armour, firepower, systems }` — the three authored hull-upgrade axes in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`. That suggests the ring data means these as *permanent hull training* rewards rather than modifiers. Candidate fixes, in order of preference:

- **(a) Hull-upgrade rewards.** Fold the grant into a hull's permanent upgrade level, feeding `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` / `resolvePlayerStrength`. Most faithful to the vocabulary, but needs a decided home for a *mutable* hull upgrade level (the hull entry's `upgrades` is authored constant data today).
- **(b) Author three modifier entries** using today's `ModifierEffect` kinds (`extra-lives`, `defence`, `defence-skill`). No model change and cheapest — but `firepower`/`systems` have no matching effect, so the entry names would misdescribe what they do. Only acceptable if the effect model is knowingly renamed to match.
- **(c) Extend `ModifierEffect`** with firepower/systems effects. New model surface for two ring-2 hexes; only if (a) is rejected.

This is a game-design decision and must be **recorded on this item before implementation** — do not pick one in code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — The chosen option (a), (b) or (c) is recorded on this item with its reasoning and the rejected alternatives, before any code is written.
- **AC2** — Each of `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade` and `firepower-up` has a modelled outcome that is visible in the hangar once owned (a named row) and survives `resolveActiveLoadout` / the defender path as applicable.
- **AC3** — The effect is **measurable**, not just ownership: capture the granting hex and assert a specific before/after change (starting lives, defence rating, or firepower) through the shipped pure rules — not merely that the id appears in an owned set.
- **AC4** — The change stays inside the ring-2 aggression-band budget (`ringAggressionBudget` / `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`) and does not trivialise ring 2; demonstrated with the existing budget tests rather than asserted.
- **AC5** — The three ids are removed from the effect-free allowlist introduced as AC5(e) of AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91, so the guard tightens rather than permanently excusing them.
- **AC6** — Existing saves already holding these ids gain the effect on load with no migration and no schema change; a save that holds none is unchanged.
- **AC7** — Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md): the change is pure rules + data, so no new `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` divergence row — or one is recorded with its reason.

## Key files
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — `hex-r2-8/9/10` grants
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:320` — the `kind: 'modifier'` fallback
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `ModifierEffect`, and `HullUpgrades` if option (a)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — `resolvePlayerStrength`, `defenderRatingFromUpgrades`, `ownedEntriesOf`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `ringAggressionBudget`
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` + `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — the timing model already names these grants and must stay consistent

## Constraints
- No second copy of an effect rule: reuse `ModifierEffect` / `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` rather than adding a parallel path.
- Do not silently drop the grants from the ring data — three hexes would then pay nothing at all.

## Risky assumptions
- That these three ids are hull training rather than generic modifiers — the naming implies it, but the ring data does not say so.
- `ringTiming.ts` records `firepower-up` in its baseline; if the chosen option changes the modelled loadout, the baseline must be regenerated deliberately, not incidentally.

## Impact
Ring 2's three upgrade hexes start paying out something the player can see and feel, instead of writing a string into a save field that changes nothing.

# Teleport tunnel VFX module

## Target outcome

As a player escaping a hopeless swarm, I see a Deep-Space-9-style wormhole tunnel open from my start position toward the resolved destination, grow rapidly, hold through transit, then collapse — so the escape is legible instead of a jarring single-frame blink.

## Definition of done

- **Pass/fail checks:** a caller can build a tunnel from a start point/heading and a resolved destination; the effect advances through ordered grow/transit/collapse phases by explicit `update(dt)`; geometry is identical for the same seed (no `Math.random`); display objects are capped; one container; `destroy()` is idempotent; each layer has an `*_ENABLE_*` toggle.
- **Automated tests:** new `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.test.ts` unit suite covers phase boundaries (grow ≈ 0.75 s, transit, collapse), growth progression, determinism across two identical plans, the display-object cap, `isComplete()` after the full duration, teardown idempotence (double `destroy()` safe) and layer toggles.

## Constraints

- Mirror `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts`: a single phased timeline is the source of truth; a deterministic seeded plan via `createSeededRng`; dt-driven, never wall-clock tweens; one container; teardown exactly once.
- No `Math.random`, no per-frame allocations, bounded display objects.
- The module must not know about the scene/registry; it exposes duration constants and a `destructionScale`/lifecycle the wiring slice applies.
- Keep it renderable above the background and below the death flash (depth consistent with the phase-shift overlays).

## Risky assumptions

- The tunnel is drawn with Phaser `Graphics` (no new binary art assets), as `backgroundWarp.ts` does; if the swirl needs a shader that is out of scope and becomes a separate work item.
- Grow duration is fixed at ≈ 0.75 s by the producer's Q1 answer; transit ≈ 0.4 s and collapse ≈ 0.25 s are exported tunables (Appendix A3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A wormhole-style tunnel is rendered from the ship's start position to the resolved destination, growing rapidly to completion, holding during transit and collapsing at the end; geometry is deterministic (no Math.random), bounded (capped display objects) and fully torn down on completion and on scene shutdown (no leaked containers or handles).
- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.ts` exports the tree-phase timeline constants (grow ≈ 0.75 s, transit, collapse) and an `update(dt)` that advances grow → transit → collapse in order and reports completion.
- Tunnel geometry is derived from the start point, heading and resolved destination with a seeded RNG (no `Math.random`), and two plans built from the same seed produce identical geometry.
- The number of display objects is capped by an exported constant and all objects live in one container torn down exactly once by completion and by `destroy()` (idempotent).
- Each visual layer has an exported `TELEPORT_TUNNEL_ENABLE_*` toggle (defaults from constants) overridable per call.
- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.test.ts` passes and covers phase boundaries, growth, determinism, the cap, completion and teardown idempotence.
- Unit tests cover the pure timeline and phase model (phase boundaries, growth, teardown idempotence, layer toggles) and integration tests cover the sequenced teleport in the game and at least one gym.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.ts` modelled on `backgroundWarp.ts`: exported phase constants, `planTeleportTunnel(...)` seeded geometry, `createTeleportTunnel(scene, opts)`, `TeleportTunnel.update(dt)` / `destroy()` / `isComplete()`.
- Add depth/duration constants to `src/core/constants.ts` if needed.
- Add the unit suite `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.test.ts`.

## Dependencies

- None (foundation slice).

## Deliverables

- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.ts`, `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.test.ts`, constants, module doc comment.

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.ts`
- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.test.ts`
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts`
- `src/core/rng.ts`

# Shared sequenced teleport seam

## Target outcome

As a player escaping a hopeless swarm, the warp reads as a deliberate three-beat transit — a grow phase, a normal-speed tunnel transit and a collapse — and the world is never left stuck in slow motion, in the game and every gym.

## Definition of done

- **Pass/fail checks:** `CombatScene.triggerTeleport()` no longer writes the position in the same frame; it resolves the destination, starts a sequence (grow → transit → collapse), defers the `player.setPosition` + movement-state sync to the transit start, exposes a `teleportTimeScale()` factor (¼ during grow, 1× elsewhere) and a grow-phase steering lock consumed by `_tickPlayer`, and tears the tunnel down on completion, pause, transition, shutdown and `resetRunState()`.
- **Automated tests:** integration tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` / `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and at least one gym assert the ordered phases, that the position only changes at transit, that the world factor returns to exactly 1× after the sequence, that the ship is not steerable during grow, and that a scene shutdown mid-sequence leaks no container.
- **Parity guard:** the new shared method(s) are registered in the repo-wide duplicate-body guard / equivalence test so they are defined exactly once, in `src/scenes/core/`.

## Constraints

- **Parity first:** one implementation in `src/scenes/core/` consumed by `PlayScene` and every teleporting gym; no divergent copies (AGENTS.md).
- Compose the teleport factor multiplicatively with the existing `enemyBulletTimeScale()` seam (Chrono Field), never replace it.
- Clear the factor on every exit path (completion, pause, shutdown, abort) so the world can never be left at ¼ speed.
- The arrival Phase Shift is granted at sequence start (preserves today's `consumeTeleport()` semantics and covers the whole ≈1.4 s animation with its 1.5 s base intangibility).
- The teleport sequence itself (tunnel update + ship transit) always advances at real time, never at ¼ speed.

## Risky assumptions

- The sequence can be driven from the shared scene tick without introducing a global time-scale framework (Appendix A4). Any generic `timeScale` framework is out of scope and becomes a separate work item.
- Pausing a scene mid-sequence is reachable only through the existing `paused` freeze; the seam must clear the factor there as it already freezes the tick.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The shared teleport seam sequences the warp as three ordered phases grow, transit and collapse, with everything except the teleport sequence at 1/4 speed during grow (enemies, enemy bullets, hazards, wave/transition timers, effect and recharge clocks, HUD countdowns and the player's input and physics), the ship not steerable during grow, the tunnel traversed at normal speed, and the world speed restored to exactly 1x when the sequence ends, in the shipped game and in every gym that teleports.
- `triggerTeleport()` starts an ordered grow (≈ 0.75 s) → transit → collapse sequence and does not move the ship until the transit begins; the resolved destination and the arrival Phase Shift grant are unchanged from today.
- `teleportTimeScale()` returns ¼ during grow, 1× during transit/collapse/afterwards, and composes multiplicatively with the existing enemy-bullet time scale.
- The ship is not steerable during grow (input is ignored by `_tickPlayer`) while the tunnel/transit advance at real time.
- Teardown is idempotent and runs on completion, pause, transition, `resetRunState()` and scene shutdown; the world factor is exactly 1× on every exit path.
- The new shared method(s) are defined exactly once repo-wide and the duplicate-body/equivalence guard passes for `PlayScene` and every teleporting gym.
- Integration tests cover the sequenced teleport in `PlayScene` and at least one gym.

## Minimal implementation

- In `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`, split `triggerTeleport()` into resolve → `_startTeleportSequence(dest)`; store the start/dest/heading and start the tunnel.
- In `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, own the tunnel handle, a phase clock, `teleportTimeScale()`, `isTeleportSteeringLocked()`, the deferred position write, and a teardown hook called from `resetRunState()`/shutdown.
- Gate `_tickPlayer` input reading with the steering lock.
- Add the guard registration and integration tests.

## Dependencies

- Teleport tunnel VFX module (builds the tunnel this seam drives).

## Deliverables

- Sequenced seam in `CombatScene`/`CombatCoreScene`, guard registration, integration tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`
- `src/vfx/teleportTunnel.ts`
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`

# World slow-motion time scale

## Target outcome

As a player, the grow phase reads as a true bullet-time beat — enemies, enemy bullets, hazards, wave/transition timers, effect and recharge clocks, HUD countdowns and the player's own physics all slow to ¼ speed, then snap back to exactly normal speed — in the shipped game and every teleporting gym.

## Definition of done

- **Pass/fail checks:** `PlayScene.tick(dt)` and every teleporting gym's tick apply `teleportTimeScale()` to a deliberate list of dt consumers, composed multiplicatively with `enemyBulletTimeScale()`; the teleport sequence's own update and the ship transit use real time; after the sequence every scaled consumer sees the exact original `dt` again.
- **Automated tests:** unit/integration tests assert (a) ¼ scaling of enemies, bullets, effect/recharge clocks, wave/transition timers, HUD countdowns and player physics during grow; (b) the factor composes with Chrono Field; (c) exactly 1× after collapse; (d) no ¼ state survives pause/transition/shutdown.

## Constraints

- **Deliberate list, not blind scaling:** apply the factor only to the consumers named in AC1/Q1=a; telemetry, audio beat clocks that must not stall, and the teleport sequence stay at real time (or are explicitly documented).
- Game↔gym parity: the game and every teleporting gym consume the same factor from the shared core; no divergent copy.
- Must not disturb the recharge/single-use timers' correctness — scaling must stop cleanly when the sequence ends.
- Pause/transition safety: the factor is cleared on every exit path.

## Risky assumptions

- The existing per-subsystem `dt` flow is the right seam (Appendix A4); no Phaser `time.timeScale` is introduced.
- HUD countdowns are refreshed from the scaled clocks, so slowing the clocks is sufficient to slow the displayed countdown; if a HUD element reads wall-clock it is folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- During grow, enemies, enemy bullets, hazards, wave/transition timers, effect clocks, recharge clocks, HUD countdowns and the player's physics advance at ¼ speed in `PlayScene` and every teleporting gym.
- The teleport tunnel and the ship's tunnel transit advance at real time (never ¼ speed).
- The teleport factor composes multiplicatively with `enemyBulletTimeScale()` with no double-scaling.
- When the sequence ends the world returns to exactly 1× — no residual factor after completion, pause, transition or shutdown.
- A shared test asserts the game and at least one gym produce identical scaled `dt` for the same phase.

## Minimal implementation

- In `PlayScene.tick(dt)`, compute `worldDt = dt * effectsRegistry.enemyBulletTimeScale() * teleportTimeScale()` and route the deliberate consumer list through it; keep the tunnel/transit on `dt`.
- In `GymFormationScene.tick` and every teleporting gym tick, apply the same composed factor to the same consumer list.
- Add the scaling/composition/restoration tests.

## Dependencies

- Shared sequenced teleport seam (provides `teleportTimeScale()` and the steering lock).

## Deliverables

- Composed world `dt` wiring in `PlayScene` and every teleporting gym, scaling tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts`

- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

# Suppress phase flash on teleport

## Target outcome

As a player, the teleport's own tunnel is the screen-wide read for the escape — the old full-screen phase flash no longer fires on a teleport-arrival Phase Shift, while a genuine Phase Shift activation still flashes.

## Definition of done

- **Pass/fail checks:** a teleport-arrival Phase Shift activation (the one granted by `consumeTeleport()`) skips **only** the full-screen flash layer; the dim / split / vignette / shimmer layers and the gameplay effect still apply; a genuine Phase Shift activation still plays the flash. The flash code, `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_FLASH` toggle and palette are retained.
- **Automated tests:** a `phaseShiftJuice` test asserts teleport-arrival suppression vs a normal activation playing the flash; a seam/integration test asserts no `flashRemainingMs` peak after a teleport.

## Constraints

- Suppress only the flash layer — never the whole Phase Shift treatment (producer Q2 = a).
- Keep the toggle/code so the effect remains available for genuine activations.
- No change to the arrival Phase Shift's duration, intangibility or gameplay semantics.
- Determinism unchanged (dt-driven, edge-triggered).

## Risky assumptions

- `consumeTeleport()`/`applyPhaseShift()` can pass a per-activation `skipFlash` flag through to `PhaseShiftJuice` without changing the public activation API for other callers; the flag defaults to false.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The teleport no longer triggers the existing full-screen phase flash (only the flash layer is suppressed; the arrival Phase Shift keeps its other layers and gameplay effect), and the flash's code plus enable toggle are retained for a genuine Phase Shift activation, pinned by a test asserting the teleport-arrival activation skips the flash while a normal activation still plays it.
- A teleport-arrival Phase Shift activation does not raise the full-screen flash (its peak alpha stays zero) while the other phase layers still activate.
- A genuine (non-teleport) Phase Shift activation still plays the full-screen flash.
- The flash implementation and `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_FLASH` toggle remain in the codebase and are exercised by the normal-activation test.
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts` (and the teleport seam test) pass with the new case.

## Minimal implementation

- Thread a `skipFlash` option from `applyPhaseShift`/`consumeTeleport` into `PhaseShiftJuice.update`/`_startPhase`.
- Add the suppression test and a genuine-activation regression test.

## Dependencies

- Shared sequenced teleport seam (identifies the teleport-arrival activation path).

## Deliverables

- Flash-suppression option in `phaseShiftJuice`, seam flag, tests.

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.test.ts`

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`

# Teleport grow and collapse SFX

## Target outcome

As a player, the escape is audible: a noisy/wobbly pitch-rising cue as the tunnel grows and a matching falling tone as it collapses, so the transit reads viscerally in the game and every gym.

## Definition of done

- **Pass/fail checks:** `playTeleportGrowSound()` fires on the grow-phase edge and `playTeleportCollapseSound()` on the collapse-phase edge, from the shared seam so the game and every gym inherit them; both are headless-safe no-ops with no audio; both are routed through the shared voice limiter; the deterministic audio build renders the WAVs and the cue-coverage contract passes.
- **Automated tests:** `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` / `effects.contract.test.ts` (or the teleport-specific contract test) assert the two cues are registered, mapped to baked assets, and no-op headless; a seam test asserts each cue fires exactly once on its phase edge.

## Constraints

- **Audio is a build artefact:** new SFX require a ToneForge recipe + `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` entry + re-rendered/verified WAVs (`npm run build-audio:render`); the browser bundle must never import ToneForge (`scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs`).
- Reuse the existing recipe/manifest/baked-WAV pipeline and the shared voice limiter; do not invent a new audio path.
- Headless tests must stay deterministic — cues degrade to no-ops without an AudioContext.

## Risky assumptions

- ToneForge can produce a pitch-rising grow recipe and a falling collapse recipe from the existing recipe vocabulary; if not, the cue family is authored as two variants of the nearest existing recipe and recorded in the mapping doc.
- `GymRechargeTuning` slider-driven frequent teleports are bounded by the shared voice limiter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dedicated teleport SFX play on grow and collapse (pitch-rising, then falling) in the game and gyms, are headless-safe no-ops without audio, and are registered in the cue manifest and recipe catalogue so the deterministic audio build and the cue-coverage contract test pass.
- Two new cues (`playTeleportGrowSound`, `playTeleportCollapseSound`) are exported from `src/audio/effects.ts`, fire from the shared teleport seam on the grow/collapse edges, and are headless-safe no-ops.
- Both cues appear in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` with ToneForge recipes and baked seeds, the WAVs are rendered and checksummed, and the cue-coverage contract test passes.
- The grow cue rises in pitch and the collapse cue falls, driven by the recipe (not per-frame synthesis in the browser).
- A seam test asserts each cue fires exactly once on its phase edge and not on other phases.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-teleport-grow.yaml` and `aihell-teleport-collapse.yaml`.
- Register both in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`; run the audio render and check in the WAVs + checksums.
- Add the cue wrappers to `src/audio/effects.ts` and call them from the shared seam's phase transitions.
- Add the contract/seam tests.

## Dependencies

- Shared sequenced teleport seam (needs the grow/collapse phase edges to fire from).

## Deliverables

- ToneForge recipes, manifest entries, baked WAVs, cue wrappers, contract + seam tests.

# Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard (test-first verification)

## Goal

*As a balancing agent, I want a measured, allocation-bounded budget for the
enemy-bullet advance **before** the Chrono field gains a per-bullet check, so the
range-limited slow cannot silently regress frame time.*

This is the plan's **test/verification first** slice: it adds only tests plus a
`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` note, changes no production behaviour, and is green on
arrival. It pins the cost budget that the per-bullet check
([Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms]) must meet.

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3 (Chrono Field nerfing), constraint
  "Performance — membership must be a squared-distance compare with no per-bullet
  allocation and no new per-frame garbage".
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts:87` `advanceWrappingBullets` is the single
  per-frame enemy-bullet hot loop (game + every gym).
- Precedent for the assertion style: AH-0MVXV0F0Y004NENT (per-frame allocation
  removal) and the hot-loop guards it added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` gains an allocation-budget test that advances a large array (≥500 bullets) through `advanceWrappingBullets` over many frames and asserts the hot loop creates no new arrays/objects per bullet (bounded heap growth, same measurement technique as the AH-0MVXV0F0Y004NENT guards).
- The test asserts a documented, stable per-frame cost budget for the current uniform-`dt` advance and fails loudly if a future change exceeds it (the number and its meaning are recorded in the test's doc comment).
- The guard is green on today's code and this item changes no production behaviour (no source edit outside tests and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`).
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` gains a one-line note that the enemy-bullet advance carries a documented allocation/cost budget enforced by this test, naming the test.
- **Parent AC9 closed by this item** — **Tests** — new/updated unit tests cover the slow curve (level 0, mid-level, cap), the radius curve, the membership maths (inside, outside, exactly on the boundary) and the active/inactive window; scene-level tests prove an inside bullet is slowed while an outside bullet is not, in the game and in each affected gym; the ring's drawn/cleared lifecycle is tested. **Full project test suite must pass** with the change (run through the test skill, never ad-hoc invocations).

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` with the allocation-budget + baseline-cost test (reusing the existing allocation-guard idiom, no new harness).
- Add the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` pointer line.
- No production code change.

## Key Files

- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` — the budget note.
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — read only (the measured seam).

None — this is the first slice and unblocks the sizing evidence for
`Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms`.

# Shared per-bullet time-scale seam

## Goal

*As an agent / gym user, I want the enemy-bullet advance to accept a per-bullet
time scale, so Chrono can slow only the bullets inside its field through one
shared implementation that the game and every gym run identically.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, constraint "**Shared-core discipline** — the
  per-bullet slowed dt belongs in `src/scenes/core/` (an optional per-bullet
  time-scale hook on `advanceWrappingBullets`) and every consumer passes the same
  resolver" and "**Backwards-compatible helper** — the per-bullet scale must be
  optional with today's uniform-dt behaviour as the default".
- Today's call sites: `PlayScene._advanceBullets` (~:5215),
  `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` (~:2183), `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690, currently raw `dt`).
- Adjacent, not in scope: **AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB — World slow-motion time scale**
  (blocked) must be able to compose its `teleportTimeScale()` multiplicatively
  with this seam; a pure, side-effect-free resolver keeps that possible. Do not
  implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `advanceWrappingBullets` accepts an **optional** per-bullet time-scale resolver (e.g. a trailing `resolveScale?: (bullet: T) => number` parameter); omitting it reproduces today's uniform-`dt` behaviour exactly, so every existing caller and test passes unchanged.
- With a resolver supplied, each bullet integrates position, ages `elapsed`, fades and expires on **its own** scaled dt inside a single call — two bullets in one call advance by different distances — so no scene can apply a scale twice.
- The resolver is consulted exactly once per bullet per call, using the bullet's pre-integration position, and the loop introduces no closure, array or object allocation per bullet (satisfied against the `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` budget test).
- Player bullets are untouched: `advancePlayerBullets` keeps its signature and behaviour, and a test asserts a Chrono-style resolver never reaches player bullets.
- The helper remains a **single** definition in `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard is extended if a new exported resolver helper appears, and it passes.
- The helper's doc comment states this is the one seam every scene uses for enemy-bullet time scaling (and the composition point for future world slow-motion).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the optional resolver parameter to `advanceWrappingBullets` and use `dt * scale` for ageing, integration, fade and expiry (one scale read per bullet, no allocation).
- Tests first: default path unchanged, per-bullet divergence, once-per-call invocation, ageing/fade coupling, player-bullet exclusion.
- Extend the equivalence guard's symbol list if a new exported helper is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — the seam (one definition).
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — the new behavioural tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body / shared-symbol guard.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` (the budget this seam must respect).

# Halve Chrono slow, add radius axis

## Goal

*As a designer, I want the Chrono slow halved and a level-scaled field radius in
the committed level catalogue, so the nerf's numbers are inspectable and a future
rebalance cannot silently restore the old potency.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, producer decisions **Q1 = B** (ship-centred circle
  whose radius grows with the level) and **Q3 = A** (halve the whole slow axis).
- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (~:953) is the
  single source; `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` resolves it;
  `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` (~:1574) derives level-up copy from the specs, so
  a new axis appears in the copy automatically.
- Target numbers: `chronoSlowFactor` 0.25 → 0.375 (`k = 0.25` unchanged);
  `chronoRadius` 150 px → 300 px (`k = 0.12`), i.e. 167 / 218 / 255 px at levels
  1 / 5 / 10. `enemyBulletTimeScale()` therefore reads 0.75 at level 0 and 0.625 at
  the cap.
- No CSV/config rows: the catalogue is the source of truth (parent assumption A7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono`'s `chronoSlowFactor` entry is `base 0.25` → `cap 0.375` on the unchanged `k = 0.25` exponential-saturation curve, with its label, description and rationale updated to describe the nerfed field.
- `chronoRadius` is added as a `PowerUpLevelVariable` (union member with a doc comment), to `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` immediately after `chronoSlowFactor`, to `PowerUpLevelStats`, and as a spec entry in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` with label, unit `px`, description, rationale and exponential-saturation `base 150` → `cap 300`, `k = 0.12`.
- `resolvePowerUpAtLevel('chrono', level)` reports both axes; unit tests pin the slow at levels 0 / 1 / 5 / 10 / cap (0.25 / 0.278 / 0.339 / 0.365 / 0.375) and the radius at levels 0 / 1 / 5 / 10 / cap (150 / 167 / 218 / 255 / 300) within a documented tolerance.
- `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` stays empty and the existing catalogue-order, curve-shape and deferred-set tests pass with the new axis present.
- While the Chrono window is active `EffectsRegistry.enemyBulletTimeScale()` reports 0.75 at level 0 and 0.625 at the cap (0.722 / 0.661 / 0.635 at levels 1 / 5 / 10) and exactly 1 when inactive; `summarisePowerUpLevelChange('chrono', n, n + 1)` reports the radius delta alongside the slow and duration deltas.
- `EffectsRegistry` exposes a level-resolved `chronoFieldRadius()` beside `forceFieldRadius()` reading the same catalogue value, as the **single radius source** for the membership test, the ring and the copy (returns the resolved radius; the window gate stays with the caller).
- **Parent AC1 closed by this item** — **Halved potency at every level** — while the Chrono window is active the level-resolved `chronoSlowFactor` is `base 0.25` → `cap 0.375` on the unchanged `k = 0.25` curve, so `enemyBulletTimeScale()` reports **0.75** at level 0 and **0.625** at the cap (and 0.722 / 0.661 / 0.635 at levels 1 / 5 / 10), replacing today's 0.5 → 0.25; unit tests pin the level-0 and cap values.
- **Parent AC2 closed by this item** — **New level-scaled radius axis** — `chronoRadius` is added to `POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` (in catalogue order beside `chronoSlowFactor` and `chronoDuration`), `PowerUpLevelStats` and `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.chrono` with a label, unit (`px`) and rationale, resolving `base 150 px → cap 300 px` on exponential-saturation `k = 0.12`; the registry exposes it, the deferred-variable set stays empty, the catalogue-order/curve-shape tests pass, and level-up change summaries report the radius delta.

## Minimal implementation

- Halve the `chronoSlowFactor` base/cap and rewrite its rationale.
- Add the `chronoRadius` axis end-to-end through the catalogue (union, ordered list, stats interface, spec).
- Add `chronoFieldRadius()` to the registry; update `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts` and the parity tests that read Chrono values.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — the catalogue (single source of truth).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `enemyBulletTimeScale()` doc/value and the new `chronoFieldRadius()`.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — curve, order, deferred and copy tests.
- `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts` — the Chrono effect assertions.

## Dependencies

None — independent of the shared seam; it unblocks
`Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms` and `Draw the Chrono active-field ring`.

# Range-limited Chrono slow in game and gyms

## Goal

*As a player, I want Chrono to slow only the bullets near my ship, so the field is
a positional dodge aid I have to fly into rather than a screen-wide brake.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, producer decisions **Q1 = B** (ship-centred,
  level-scaled radius) and **A3** (inclusive boundary, matching
  `dangerDetection.isWithinRadiusSq`: `dx² + dy² <= radiusSq`).
- Replaces the single global scalar (today `dt * enemyBulletTimeScale()` at
  `PlayScene.ts:5215` and `GymFormationScene.ts:2183`, and **no scale at all** in
  `GymPowerUpsCombat` ~:690 — a pre-existing parity gap this item closes).
- Inclusive-boundary precedent: `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts:37`
  `isWithinRadiusSq`.
- Adjacent, not in scope: AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB (world slow-motion) must be able to
  multiply its own scale into this seam later — keep the resolver pure and
  composable; do not implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure, hot-loop-safe membership resolver in `src/scenes/core/` returns the slowed scale when a bullet's squared distance from the **player ship** is `<= radiusSq` (inclusive: a bullet exactly on the radius counts as inside) and exactly `1.0` outside, with no allocation, no per-bullet closure and no easing or hysteresis at the boundary; unit tests cover inside, outside and exactly-on-the-boundary.
- `PlayScene._advanceBullets` passes the per-bullet resolver, anchored on `this.player`, through the shared seam; a scene test proves one inside bullet advances at the slowed step while an outside bullet advances at exactly `dt` in the same frame, at level 0 and at the cap.
- `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` uses the identical resolver and radius (inherited by every formation gym) with no duplicated body, and its test proves the same inside/outside behaviour.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._advanceEnemyBullets` now runs the same seam (closing its pre-existing "no Chrono scale" divergence), and its test proves inside-slow / outside-normal.
- Membership is re-evaluated every frame from current positions: a test moves a bullet from outside to inside and back and proves the step changes on that frame with no sticky or accumulated scale and no double application; a slowed bullet's lifetime/fade still stretch exactly as today (ageing on the scaled dt).
- The resolver stays composable with a multiplicative outer time scale (so AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB needs no rewrite), `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard passes naming the new shared resolver, and `gymParityDocs.test.ts` passes.
- **Parent AC3 closed by this item** — **Range-limited slow** — only enemy bullets whose position lies **inside** the current radius (measured from the **player ship**, inclusive boundary: a bullet exactly on the radius counts as inside) are slowed; every enemy bullet outside advances at exactly **1.0×** normal speed. Verified in the game **and** in each gym that advances enemy bullets (AC5).
- **Parent AC4 closed by this item** — **Per-frame re-evaluation** — membership is computed from each bullet's current position every frame: a bullet entering or leaving the field changes speed on that frame, with no accumulated or sticky scale, no double-application, and no change to lifetime/fade accounting beyond the slowed ageing the effect already applies (a slowed bullet still ages on the scaled dt, so its lifetime stretches exactly as today).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the pure resolver (squared-distance compare, one call per bullet) to the shared core next to the bullet-lifecycle seam.
- Wire `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymPowerUpsCombat` to it, anchored on each scene's player.
- Tests first: resolver unit tests (inside/outside/boundary/per-frame), then the three scene tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/` — the new shared membership resolver beside `bulletLifecycle.ts`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_advanceBullets` ~:5215), `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (~:8552).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:2183) and its test.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690) and its test.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body guard.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.test.ts` (:338) — the existing Chrono-effect assertion may need updating.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Shared per-bullet time-scale seam` (the hook this wiring consumes).
- Blocked by `Halve Chrono slow, add radius axis` (the radius and slow values it reads).

# Chrono nerf acceptance verification

## Goal

*As a producer reviewing the Chrono nerf, I want one consolidated, reproducible
verification pass across the game, the gyms, the guards, the docs and the frame
budget, so the item's nine acceptance criteria are proven rather than asserted.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3 — the acceptance gate before the parent reaches
  `in_review`.
- Tests must be run through the **test skill** (`run_tests.py`), never ad-hoc;
  the full suite is enforced at the dev-push gate.
- The 50-enemy performance ceiling is measured with the project's `perf-sweep`
  skill (`.pi/skills/perf-sweep/SKILL.md`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The full project suite passes through the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope full`) with no failures and no skipped Chrono tests, and the result is recorded as a comment on this item.
- `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and `gymParityDocs.test.ts` pass with the new shared seam named, and a repo check confirms no scene holds a duplicated scaling body.
- A `perf-sweep` run records a playable enemy ceiling no worse than the pre-change baseline (both numbers recorded), confirming the per-bullet membership check did not cost frame time.
- A per-AC evidence table (parent AC1–AC9 → the test/file/command that proves it) is recorded as a comment, with any residual gap called out explicitly rather than glossed.
- Any discovered defect is filed as a child `discovered-from` item rather than fixed inside this verification item.
- **Parent AC9 closed by this item** — **Tests** — new/updated unit tests cover the slow curve (level 0, mid-level, cap), the radius curve, the membership maths (inside, outside, exactly on the boundary) and the active/inactive window; scene-level tests prove an inside bullet is slowed while an outside bullet is not, in the game and in each affected gym; the ring's drawn/cleared lifecycle is tested. **Full project test suite must pass** with the change (run through the test skill, never ad-hoc invocations).

## Minimal implementation

- Run the test skill full scope; run the perf sweep; collate the AC evidence table.
- No production code changes (verification only; a genuine defect becomes its own item).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene` tests, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts`.
- `.pi/skills/perf-sweep/SKILL.md` — the ceiling measurement.

- Blocked by `Update Chrono copy and docs` (the last implementation slice).

# Pure detail model builder for centre panel

Build the pure model function that returns detail content for any focusable row key — a heading plus body lines sourced from the catalogue, economy verdicts, and deployment builder.

## Goal

Create `buildHangarDetail(screenModel, key)` that returns, for any focusable row key, a heading plus body lines:
- The catalogue description
- Kind-specific facts (hull stats, weapon matchup, modifier effect, power-up state)
- Economy price/state verdicts (price, owned, gated, unaffordable, upgradable, capped, blocked)
- For no-focus fallback: the deployment summary from buildHangarDeployment

## Acceptance Criteria

- A detail entry exists for every row kind: unlock rows, hulls, weapons, modifiers, power-ups, saved builds, deploy, map, restart, buildout
- Every unlock state is covered: owned, buyable, gated, unaffordable, upgradable, upgrade-unaffordable, capped, blocked
- Moving focus (keyboard tab/arrows, and pointer hover) onto any hangar row triggers the detail builder which updates the centre detail panel that names the option and shows its detail: the catalogue description, the option's kind-specific facts (a hull's base defence, upgrade levels, run stats and granted skill; a weapon's matchup verdict and permanent level/cap; a modifier's effect in words; a power-up's installed/off/blocked state, level and cap), and its price / owned / gated / shortfall state — every fact sourced from the shipped catalogue and the existing pure economy verdicts, with no new gameplay number invented in the screen
- The no-focus fallback returns the deployment summary (hull, weapons, modifiers, power-ups, target hex) built by the existing pure deployment builder, so the panel can never describe a launch the screen does not perform
- All content is pure — no Phaser dependencies, fully table-testable
- A new test file hangarScreen.detail.test.ts contains table tests covering every row kind and state
- Full test suite passes

## Constraints

- No new gameplay numbers authored — all facts sourced from existing catalogue, economy, and deployment builders
- The detail model is part of the HangarScreenModel (pure), not computed inside the renderer
- CVD-safe: no information conveyed by colour alone; state words/markers accompany every tint

## Key Files

- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts — new buildHangarDetail function, integrated into HangarScreenModel
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.detail.test.ts (new) — table tests for the detail builder

## Dependencies

None (depends on existing catalogue, economy, deployment builders — all already present)

## Risks

- Row-width regression: three columns at 960px cannot hold full labels; row labels will be shortened (addressed in child 5)
- Two sources of matchup truth: detail must read the row's own model field, never re-resolve the matchup

# Section rect table and framed three-column layout for hangar screen

- Create `HANGAR_SECTION_RECTS` — a single-source rect table with one `{ key, heading, rect }` per section, in reading order

- Pin non-overlap / row-fit / in-frame layout in tests
